Canonical GUI flow to prove a candidate NC against a golden: (1) activate the File Compare tab; (2) File Compare > Compare File with File, picking candidate + golden via the Open dialog (or Compare with File if the candidate is already open); (3) Go To > Next/Previous Difference (Ctrl+Down/Ctrl+Up) to walk the diff set, bounded by Go to First/Last Difference; (4) Other > Save Compare File to export differing lines to a .txt that PRISM reads back on the file channel to assert zero/expected deltas. For a TRUE byte-exact golden prove, all Ignore Options should be OFF; for an executable-equivalence prove (tolerating N-renumber, spacing, timestamp comments, +/zero formatting) they should be ON selectively. 'Show all differences (No editing)' is the safest setup for a non-mutating prove pass. Note Ignore Comments depends on Comment start/end chars defined in the Machine Template (setupmachine.htm), so that template must be correctly associated with the file type first.

clusters.postProvingNotes: This cluster is the literal SHIP step of post-proving — once a post processor's NC output is byte-verified against a golden, this is how PRISM drip-feeds it to a real machine. Strongest blind path: author a .setup scanning sidecar (setup.scanning.commands, channel:file) with TOOL/HOLDER/WORKPIECE/FIXTURE/WCS directives — CIMCO reads it on simulation start, zero GUI. Direct file loads also exist: backplot.solid.stl, backplot.solid.dxf, backplot.gm.add-stock / add-fixture / add-workpiece (all channel:file). Parametric box/cylinder via backplot.solid.cylinder/dimensions is uia.

SET WORK OFFSETS. Deterministic blind route = WCS lines (IDs 0-6) inside the .setup scanning sidecar (channel:file). GUI fallback: backplot.gm.work-offsets / backplot.gm.work-origin (uia), or backplot.gm.detect-from-machine-def to auto-align origin once a model is loaded. Persist the whole scene with backplot.gm.save-setup (channel:file) so it auto-loads next backplot.
ENSURE UNITS MATCH (UNITS-FIRST doctrine): setup.machine.toolpath-unit (channel:file) must match the NC G20/G21 or a 25.4x scale error invalidates all collision/limit geometry.
blockers: The operator's literal phrase 'use SYSTEM machine models' maps to setup.machine-models.install which is GUI-only with NO documented .mcfg path — system-model provisioning is UIA-bound (or one-time human pre-install). Only CUSTOM-machine provisioning is truly file-blind.

GUI Geometry Manager surfaces (backplot.gm.*) only appear AFTER a backplot/sim is opened — implicit precondition: load NC + open Backplot first. The .setup/scanning file path avoids this ordering dependency.

Machine config files live under \AppData\Roaming\...\MachineCfg\ but the exact path segment + on-disk schema are undocumented — file-channel authoring of a custom machine requires reverse-engineering an installed config.

criticalProcedures.name: run-machine-simulation
criticalProcedures.channel: uia (entirely — no file/cli/dnc-api fallback for the run or verdict)
steps: PRECONDITIONS (file/uia): installed machine model (setup.backplot.machine-setup / backplot.machine-sim.install-machine-model), correct Control Type (setup.backplot.control-type / backplot.controltype.control-type), correct units+dialect (setup.machine.toolpath-unit), Arc Type = 'As in G-code' (sim.settings.arc-type), Fast engine (sim.engine.fast), and scene geometry from load-machine-model+stock. Control Type mismatch silently invalidates the entire run.

ENABLE Machine Simulation (sim.machine-simulation, uia) for kinematic collision+limit checking, then start via backplot.file.machine-simulation or backplot.file.backplot. Enable backplot.solid.simulate for material removal.

CONFIGURE the four collision settings (all uia, exact 1:1 ids): Find-All-per-model = sim.collision.per-model; tool/workpiece = sim.collision.tool-workpiece; step size = sim.collision.step-size; cutter allowance = sim.collision.cutter-allowance. Set Stop Conditions (backplot.toolpath.stop-collision, stop-travel-limits, etc.) so the sim halts deterministically at the first violation.
RUN with deterministic halting; on large programs invoke sim.report.check-collision-limit (uia) to force a fresh collision pass.
blockers: The entire run+verdict half is UIA-ONLY — no file/cli/dnc-api channel for the Machine Simulation toggle, the Collision Settings dialog, or the Simulation Report. REQUIRES the live licensed CIMCO Edit app driven by UI Automation; cannot run headless.
No documented CLI/exe args to launch backplot/machine-simulation or run Stop Conditions headless anywhere in the help pages.
tabbackplot.htm does NOT exist in the extraction (confirmed via Glob) — the Backplot-tab landing/entry overview is unverified; drive via the named sibling surfaces instead.
Geometry Manager scene (stock/fixture/workpiece) must be set first or collision detection is meaningless — it is a scene-setup dependency outside the three runtime steps.

criticalProcedures.name: read-simulation-report
steps: PRECONDITIONS (load-bearing, set first or the report is empty/misleadingly clean): sim.settings.report-errors ON, sim.report.show-errors ON (sim.report.show-warning for warnings), and sim.machine-simulation ON to populate collision + axis-limit rows at all.

READ the Simulation Report grid (sim.report, uia) — columns LINE / TYPE / DESCRIPTION / ACTION plus collision + limit + error rows. On large programs invoke sim.report.check-collision-limit first to force-populate. Cross-check axis travel live via backplot.view.show-axis-control (red on over-travel). For geometry correctness use backplot.solid.stock-compare (color-mapped gouge/leftover/in-tol).

DERIVE pass/fail (agent-side logic over the read rows — no dedicated oracle surface): zero collision/limit/error rows within tolerance = pass. Jump to any offending block with backplot.find.goto-line-block (Ctrl+J) to inspect the NC line.
blockers: ENTIRELY uia-channel — sim.report is explicitly 'GUI-only, must be read via UIA, no documented export/file'. No .json/.csv/.txt report dump exists.
Detail page backplotsimulationreport.htm is referenced repeatedly but is NOT in the extracted cluster — exact report field structure is only partially captured.

RISK: if the report grid is a custom-drawn control that does not surface row/cell text via UIA, this path silently degrades to screenshot-only. Recommend a UIA probe of the actual report control before trusting automated reads.
nc.info.toolpath-statistics (file/CSV) is only an INDIRECT limit cross-check (per-tool X/Y/Z travel ranges) — it does NOT substitute for the collision/error report.

criticalProcedures.name: file-compare-vs-golden
criticalProcedures.channel: file (Ignore Options + recommended off-GUI byte-diff) / uia (the in-app diff itself) / file (save-compare-file .txt result)
steps: DECIDE compare mode by pre-writing Ignore Options on disk per File Type (channel:file via .mcfg): filecompare.setup.ignore-block-numbers / ignore-white-spaces / ignore-comments / ignore-case / ignore-numeric-format. ALL OFF = true byte-exact golden prove; selectively ON = executable-equivalence prove (tolerate N-renumber, spacing, timestamp comments, +/zero formatting). Prefer pre-writing the config file over toggling checkboxes blind.

RUN the compare: activate filecompare.tab, then filecompare.file.compare-file-with-file (pick candidate + golden) or filecompare.file.compare-with-file if candidate is already open. Use filecompare.setup.show-all-differences for a safe non-mutating pass.

WALK + EXTERNALIZE the diff: filecompare.goto.next-difference / previous-difference (Ctrl+Down/Ctrl+Up), bounded by first/last-difference, then filecompare.other.save-compare-file (channel exported as .txt of differing lines) — the ONLY documented way to externalize CIMCO's diff result. PRISM reads the .txt back on the file channel; empty/expected = pass.

CLASSIFY semantic vs cosmetic by TWO-PASS inference (no labeled report exists): run strict (all ignores OFF) and cosmetic-tolerant (ignores ON), take the delta. Differences surviving the cosmetic pass are semantic.
blockers: The diff engine itself (compare render + Go-To walk) is UIA-only and requires the live licensed app; there is NO file/CLI diff-engine channel.
filecompare.sync.sync-left / sync-right MUTATE files (copy a diff between panes) — must NOT be used in a read-only golden prove; flag as edit-capable.
Semantic-vs-cosmetic is inferred via two-pass, not a single oracle. save-compare-file .txt has no documented schema — parse heuristically (lines-with-differences).
ignore-comments depends on Machine Template comment start/end chars (setupmachine.htm, referenced but outside this cluster) — that template must be associated with the file type first.

STRONGEST blind path actually bypasses these GUI surfaces: diff candidate vs golden .nc directly on disk off-GUI, and reserve CIMCO's in-app compare only when its NC-aware ignore semantics are specifically wanted.

criticalProcedures.name: dnc-drip-feed
criticalProcedures.channel: dnc-api (FTP — preferred, raw byte-fidelity) / file (DNC config) / uia (serial — GUI-only)
steps: WRITE the DNC machine-config on disk first (channel:file): dnc.setup / dnc.setup.protocol / dnc.setup.machine-type set protocol/port/baud/parity/dirs; for serial, dnc.serial.port / dnc.serial.directories. CRITICAL: dnc.serial.transmit can MUTATE the stream (CR/LF rewrite, remove whitespace, replace tabs, omit lines, remove ASCII 0's, start/end triggers) — set to pass-through or the machine receives different bytes than the golden. Set 'Wait for Start button' OFF for unattended ship.

FTP PUSH (preferred — verbatim raw file transfer, no stream mutation): drive ftp.split-window.send (PUT, channel:dnc-api) against the same server-address/username/password/server-default-path captured from dnc.ftp.port. Fully replicable headless via a standard FTP client.

VERIFY round-trip byte fidelity: ftp.split-window.receive (GET) the landed file back and byte-compare to the golden; ftp.split-window.refresh / list to confirm it landed. This GET-and-compare is the cleanest ship-fidelity proof.

SERIAL fallback (only if no FTP): drive the Transmit Status dialog (trans.send-status, dnc-api) + read trans.send-status.terminal (uia) which echoes exact bytes sent + bytes-sent/progress. PRECONDITION: a DNC license is required for all DNC operations.
blockers: Serial drip-feed (Transmit Status dialog) has NO documented file/CLI/dnc-api hook for the LIVE byte stream — it is GUI-only; blind serial ship requires UIA to click Start/Stop and scrape the Terminal Window. No headless serial-send command exists.

DNC-Max / SQL (MariaDB) datastore is NOT referenced in any extracted page — the dnc-api channel here is the in-editor FTP client only, NOT a DNC-Max API or DB schema. No SQL surface exists anywhere in the map.
No CLI invocation (exe+args) documented to launch a transmission/select machine/start send-receive headlessly.

synthesis.postProvingReadiness: PRISM can drive CIMCO to prove a post roughly 60-70% of the way end-to-end TODAY, with a clean split along the channel axis. surfaces.label: Assembly Design tab
surfaces.action: Shows nested components (holder contains cutter); hover highlights in preview, click selects, double-click edits. Per-component actions: Edit Component, Select Component (Replace), Remove Component, Create New Component.

surfaces.label: Assembly Details tab
surfaces.action: Sets assembly metadata and kinematics: Description, ID, Item number, Cutter point, and Orientation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Cutter point + Orientation define where the tool tip/comp point sits relative to the NC coordinates — wrong values shift the toolpath in sim, so they must match the post's expected comp/orientation to prove the program traces correctly.
fields: Cutter point (Milling: Center / Tip compensation point)

surfaces.label: Editing assembly window
surfaces.action: Window to configure an assembly = holder containing a cutter. Save / Save as / Cancel buttons sit lower-right of the preview; Escape cancels.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The assembly is the full holder+cutter stack the sim uses for holder-collision and clearance checks; proving a post needs the assembly fully built (both components defined and STL-complete) for valid collision results.

surfaces.label: Axes support (X, Y, Z, A, B, C)
surfaces.action: Indicators showing which axes are supported by the currently selected Machine Setup.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Confirms the selected machine supports the axes the post output commands (e.g. 4th/5th axis A/B/C) before proving a multi-axis program.

surfaces.label: Control Type
surfaces.action: Dropdown to select the control type of the machine to simulate; per-file-type control type configurable in Backplot section of Editor Setup.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Selecting the correct control type makes the backplot interpret the dialect the post emits; wrong control type yields false sim errors, so this is a precondition for a valid prove-out.

surfaces.label: Machine (Machine Setup)
surfaces.action: Dropdown to select the machine setup to simulate; must be selected before starting Backplot/Machine Simulation. Bundled machines show '(Bundled)'. Per-file-type machine setup configurable in Backplot Editor Setup.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Loads the kinematic machine model used for collision + travel-limit checking; choosing the actual target machine is mandatory to prove the post output on that machine's geometry and limits.

surfaces.label: Backplot
surfaces.action: Simulate the current open NC program; opens the simulation window with NC code (left), simulation (center), Geometry Manager docking pane (right).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Primary entry point to run a backplot simulation of a generated NC program; needed to visually prove the post output runs and to surface the Geometry Manager / Navigation / Simulation tabs that report collisions, limits, and toolpath integrity.

surfaces.label: Backplot File
surfaces.action: Backplot an NC file directly from disk without opening it first (NC code is not shown); dropdown arrow lists recently opened programs.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent point the simulator at a golden / candidate NC file straight off disk, the cleanest blind path to load a specific post output for proving without GUI file-open navigation.

surfaces.label: Backplot Setup
surfaces.action: Open the Backplot configuration dialog in the Editor Setup (control-type & machine-setup per file type configuration).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Configures which control type / machine model is associated with a file type; pre-condition so the right machine is loaded automatically when proving a post.

surfaces.label: Close Backplot
surfaces.action: Close the simulation window / backplot session.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Teardown step to release the simulation between successive prove-out runs of different NC files.

surfaces.label: Machine Simulation
surfaces.action: Simulate the current NC program in full Machine Simulation (shows machine head/table/base models); licensed add-on, only visible with a valid Machine Simulation license.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Machine Simulation enables collision detection and axis travel-limit errors during the run; the Simulation Report then includes collision + limit-error info, directly proving a post does not crash the machine or exceed travel.

surfaces.label: Find
surfaces.action: Search (and replace) through the active file; same as Find under the Editor tab.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent locate a specific G/M-code or coordinate in the post output during prove-out to correlate with a sim event.

surfaces.label: Find Next
surfaces.action: Find the next match in the active file (same as Editor tab).

surfaces.label: Find Previous
surfaces.action: Find the previous match in the active file (same as Editor tab).

surfaces.label: Go to Line/Block Number
surfaces.path: Backplot > Find > Go to Line/Block Number
surfaces.action: Jump to a specified line or block (N) number in the active file (same as Editor tab).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Jumps the editor to the NC block flagged by a stop condition / sim halt, linking a prove-out failure to its exact line in the post output.

surfaces.label: Next Tool Change
surfaces.action: Jump to the next tool change in the file (same as Editor tab).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Navigates the post output tool change by tool change for per-tool prove-out review.

surfaces.label: Previous Tool Change
surfaces.action: Jump to the previous tool change in the file (same as Editor tab).

surfaces.label: Fixtures / Add Fixture
surfaces.action: Add a fixture from an STL file (right-click > Add Fixture > open STL); appears under Fixtures with editable properties.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Loading the real fixture STL lets the prove-out detect tool/holder-to-fixture collisions in the post output; file-driven fixture provisioning.

surfaces.label: Stock / Add Stock (Rectangle/Cylinder/STL/DXF)
surfaces.action: Add one stock (right-click > Add Stock) as STL, DXF, Cylinder, or Box (Dimensions / Min-Max); appears in Geometry Manager with type-specific properties and reveals the True Vision panel.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Stock is mandatory for material-removal prove-out; STL/DXF stock is file-driven, box/cylinder is parametric; defines the raw material the post output machines.

surfaces.label: Workpieces / Add Workpiece
surfaces.action: Add a workpiece (design model) from a file (right-click > Add Workpiece > open); appears under Workpieces with editable properties.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The Workpiece is the golden design STL used by Stock Compare; loading it is the prerequisite for the gouge/leftover-material geometry comparison of the post output.

surfaces.label: Base
surfaces.action: Shows the machine base and its associated axes (Machine Simulation only); right-click to set visibility; editable via Machine Configuration Editor; carries Default Origin.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Base + Default Origin anchor the machine model in space for collision/origin prove-out.

surfaces.label: Copy Position
surfaces.path: Geometry Manager > right-click element > Copy Position
surfaces.action: Copy an element's Translation and Rotation properties.

surfaces.label: Cross Section View
surfaces.path: Geometry Manager > right-click stock > Cross Section
surfaces.action: Slice the stock along an axis; drag the coordinate-system arrows to move the slice; opens the Cross Section Plane Panel; includes a stock/workpiece compare option; OFF disables. Fast version only.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Cross-sectioning the machined stock against the workpiece reveals interior gouges/leftover material the post output produced that surface views miss; interior geometry prove-out.

surfaces.label: Detect from machine definition
surfaces.path: Geometry Manager > right-click Work Origin > Detect from machine definition
surfaces.action: Copy the XYZ position of the Work Origin from the machine definition (Base > Default Origin in Machine Config Editor).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Auto-aligns the work origin to the machine's defined default origin so the prove-out datum matches the real machine.

surfaces.label: Head
surfaces.action: Shows the machine head and its associated axes (Machine Simulation only); right-click to set visibility; editable via Machine Configuration Editor.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Head kinematics participate in collision/travel checks during prove-out of multi-axis post output.

surfaces.label: Paste Position
surfaces.path: Geometry Manager > right-click element > Paste Position
surfaces.action: Paste previously copied Translation and Rotation properties onto an element.

surfaces.label: Regenerate
surfaces.action: Regenerate (refresh) the solid stock model at the current NC position. Standard version only.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Forces the machined-stock result to recompute at the current block so the prove-out reflects the true post-output state at that point.

surfaces.label: Remove
surfaces.action: Remove a selected element from the simulation environment (if removable).

surfaces.label: Save Setup
surfaces.action: Save the entire setup (elements + tool data) to a .setup file (by default next to the NC program); auto-loaded when starting Backplot. Governed by Scanning config.

surfaces.label: Save STL file
surfaces.path: Geometry Manager > right-click stock > Save STL file
surfaces.action: Save the machined stock (as shown at the current NC position) to an STL file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Exports the simulated machined result of the post output to STL for off-GUI mesh-diff against a golden part; a concrete geometry mesh comparison.

surfaces.label: Select origin in simulation
surfaces.path: Geometry Manager > right-click Work Origin > Select origin in simulation
surfaces.action: Highlight the Work Origin in the simulation (white point + RGB axes); drag axes to reposition the origin directly; XYZ shows in the Workpiece position panel.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent visually confirm/adjust where the post output's program zero lands on the part/stock.

surfaces.label: Table
surfaces.action: Shows the machine table and its associated axes (Machine Simulation only); right-click to set visibility; editable via Machine Configuration Editor.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Table kinematics participate in collision/travel checks during prove-out.

surfaces.action: Set a selected element to Visible, Hidden, or Transparent.

surfaces.action: Adjust work offsets via Translation and Rotation properties.

surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines machine kinematics/limits/default origin used for the prove-out; .MacBundle files are file-installable, enabling blind provisioning of a target machine for post verification.

surfaces.label: Install Machine Model (Editor Setup)
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > Machine Models > install machine
surfaces.action: Install the machine you want to simulate (step 1 of Machine Simulation setup); downloaded machines show '(Bundled)'.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Installing the target machine model is the prerequisite that makes collision/limit prove-out against that machine possible.

surfaces.label: Scan for navigation information
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > Scanning > Scan for navigation information
surfaces.action: Enable scanning so the Navigation tab is populated; structure/keywords configured in Editor Setup > Navigation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Prerequisite to populate the Navigation tree used to verify post-output program structure.

surfaces.label: Export as DXF File
surfaces.path: Backplot > Other > Export as DXF File
surfaces.action: Export the toolpath data as a DXF (vector) file; configurable in Other section of Editor Setup.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Exports the simulated toolpath geometry to a DXF that can be diffed/measured off-GUI against a golden toolpath, a file-channel geometry comparison of the post output.

surfaces.label: Full Screen
surfaces.action: Show the simulation window in full screen; exit with Escape or right-click menu.

surfaces.label: Other Setup
surfaces.action: Open the Other setup dialog in the Editor Setup (incl. DXF export configuration).

surfaces.label: Save Presentation
surfaces.action: Export the entire simulation as a stand-alone Simulation File or a Presentation Bundle (includes the Presentation Viewer app); usable without CIMCO Edit and for sending setups to CIMCO support.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Captures a self-contained record of a prove-out run (simulation file) that can be archived alongside the NC program / setup sheet as evidence the post output simulated cleanly.

surfaces.label: Add Stock
surfaces.action: Insert a default rectangular stock model based on toolpath data; if Scanning is enabled, stock type/dimensions can be auto-scanned from the NC program or its Setup file. Down arrow shows more options.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Stock is required for solid material-removal simulation; auto-scanning stock from the NC program / setup file is the blind path to set up a faithful machined-result prove-out.

surfaces.label: Cylinder
surfaces.action: Insert a cylinder-shaped stock defined by center position, diameter and height with definable Axis and Origin (no Scanning).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Round/bar stock for lathe or cylindrical-part prove-out.

surfaces.label: Dimensions
surfaces.action: Insert a rectangular stock sized from toolpath data; defined by height, width, length centered on an XYZ origin (no Scanning).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines a box stock for material-removal prove-out without depending on scan config.

surfaces.label: DXF
surfaces.action: Load and insert stock from a DXF file into the simulation (no Scanning).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Loads a 2D-profile stock from DXF for prove-out; file-driven.

surfaces.label: Min/Max
surfaces.action: Insert a rectangular stock defined by two points (Lower Corner and Upper Corner) in XYZ (no Scanning).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines a box stock by explicit corner coordinates for prove-out.

surfaces.label: Reset Zoom
surfaces.action: Reset the simulation window after using Zoom Window or Zoom Selection (show entire stock). Fast version only.

surfaces.label: Simulate
surfaces.action: Enable continuous solid material-removal update of the stock during playback (Fast version); Standard version always updates and this regenerates the solid model at the current NC position. Requires a stock model.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Turns on true material-removal simulation, the basis for proving the machined result of the post output matches the design (feeds Stock Compare).

surfaces.label: STL
surfaces.action: Load and insert stock from an STL file into the simulation (no Scanning).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Loads a near-net / cast stock STL so material-removal prove-out matches real incoming stock; file-driven, no GUI dimensioning.

surfaces.label: Stock Compare
surfaces.action: Color-code the machined stock by distance to a design-model Workpiece (STL): red=over-machined/gouge, blue=under-machined, green=in-tolerance; hover shows distance. Fast version only. Requires Stock + Workpiece in Geometry Manager.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The strongest visual prove: compares the machined-stock result of the post output against a golden design STL and flags gouges (red) / leftover material (blue), a near byte-compare of geometry. Tolerances set on the Simulation tab.

surfaces.label: Zoom Selection (stock accuracy)
surfaces.action: Increase stock accuracy within a user-dragged rectangular area (click-hold-drag-release). Fast version only; reset via Reset Zoom.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Localized high-accuracy material-removal verification of a selected region.

surfaces.label: Zoom Window
surfaces.action: Increase stock simulation accuracy by creating a cut-out of the stock covering the window. Fast version only; reset via Reset Zoom.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Higher-accuracy local material-removal check on a feature of the post output (e.g. a tight pocket).

surfaces.label: Geometry Manager Tab
surfaces.path: Backplot > docking pane > Geometry Manager tab
surfaces.action: Set up the simulation environment: origin, offsets, workpiece, fixture, machine models (Head/Table/Base), and stock. Upper area lists elements, lower area shows properties of the selected element. Right-click for element options.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Central setup surface for a faithful prove-out; defines work origin/offsets, fixtures, design workpiece, and stock that the post output is simulated against; correct setup here is what makes collision/Stock-Compare results trustworthy.

surfaces.label: Navigation Tab
surfaces.action: Tree-menu overview of the NC program's contents during simulation; selecting a keyword jumps to the matching NC line and vice versa. Right-click to expand/collapse all levels. Only visible/updated while Backplot is active.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Maps post-output structure (tool changes, operations, keywords) into a navigable tree so an agent can confirm the expected program structure was emitted and jump to any section during prove-out.

surfaces.label: Simulation Report / Settings (Simulation tab)
surfaces.action: With Machine Simulation, the Simulation tab's report includes collision and limit-error info plus a Collision Settings section; also hosts Stock Compare settings (Compare range, Stock to leave).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The Simulation Report is the readable pass/fail summary of a prove-out; collisions, limit errors, and Stock-Compare tolerances all surface here; an agent reads this (UIA element text) to decide if the post output passed. Detail page backplotsimulationreport.htm is not in this cluster's list.

surfaces.label: Variables Tab
surfaces.action: Show initial variable state (upper) and current state / Watch List (lower) for the NC program; variables auto-detected. Initial values can be edited in-place to test without changing the NC code.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent inspect and override macro variables the post output uses (e.g. parametric values) and watch their evaluated values through the run; proves macro/variable logic the post emitted resolves correctly.

surfaces.label: Show All Tools
surfaces.action: If multiple tools are used, keep each visible throughout the simulation.

surfaces.label: Show/Hide Tool
surfaces.action: Show or hide the simulation tool; down arrow exposes additional tool display options.

surfaces.label: Show Tool Colors
surfaces.action: Show the tool colors.

surfaces.label: Show Tool Holder
surfaces.action: Show the tool holder in the simulation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Showing the holder lets holder-to-stock collisions become visible; pairs with the Holder To Stock stop condition to prove post-emitted clearances/retracts protect the holder.

surfaces.label: Show Tool Transparent
surfaces.action: Render the tool transparently.

surfaces.label: Show Tool Vector
surfaces.action: Show the tool vector (orientation axis).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Tool vector visualization helps verify multi-axis tool orientation emitted by the post (A/B/C moves point the tool correctly).

surfaces.label: Tool Setup (Tool Manager)
surfaces.action: Open the Tool Manager to view/modify tools in the NC program, configure tool types, colors, geometry; tool data persists to a tool library.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Tool geometry (length/diameter/holder) drives collision + gouge accuracy; correct tool definitions are required for a faithful prove-out of the post output. Tool library files can be edited off-GUI.

surfaces.label: Tool 1-N
surfaces.action: Per-tool checkboxes to show/hide each individual tool used in the program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Confirms the set of tools the post output actually invokes (one checkbox per tool number), a quick tool-count cross-check against the program.

surfaces.label: Animate / Show Remaining Toolpath Dimmed
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate / Show Remaining Toolpath Dimmed
surfaces.action: Run the simulation while dimming the unprocessed part of the toolpath.

surfaces.label: Remember Animation Mode Between Sessions
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Remember Animation Mode Between Sessions
surfaces.action: Persist the chosen animation Mode after Backplot is closed and reopened.

surfaces.label: Animate / Show Current Z-Level
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate / Show Current Z-Level
surfaces.action: Show the current toolpath at the current Z-level.

surfaces.label: Animate / Show Entire Z-Level
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate / Show Entire Z-Level
surfaces.action: Show all toolpaths at the current Z-level.

surfaces.label: Animate / Show From Last Rapid
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate / Show From Last Rapid
surfaces.action: Hide toolpaths preceding the previous rapid move at any point in the simulation.

surfaces.label: Animate / Show From Last Tool Change
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate / Show From Last Tool Change
surfaces.action: Hide toolpaths preceding the previous tool change at any point in the simulation.

surfaces.label: Animate / Show From start
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate / Show From start
surfaces.action: Begin simulation showing only the initial segment; subsequent toolpaths appear progressively as machining unfolds.

surfaces.label: Animate / Show Tail
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate / Show Tail
surfaces.action: Show only a trailing part of the toolpath following the tool.

surfaces.label: Animate / Show To End
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate / Show To End
surfaces.action: Begin showing all toolpaths, then gradually hide completed sections.

surfaces.label: Animate Tool Only
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Mode > Animate Tool Only
surfaces.action: Show the entire toolpath while animating only the tool.

surfaces.label: Hide Toolpath
surfaces.action: Hide the entire toolpath.

surfaces.label: Highlight Arcs
surfaces.action: Highlight arc (G02/G03) movements in the toolpath.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Arc highlighting exposes how the post translated arcs (IJK vs R, plane selection), a frequent post-bug surface; mis-emitted arcs show as wrong-radius highlights.

surfaces.label: Highlight Element
surfaces.action: Highlight the current toolpath element sequentially as the program runs (enables Zoom To Highlighted).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Highlighting the active element links each NC block to its geometry, letting an agent attribute a sim anomaly to a specific emitted line.

surfaces.label: Large Points
surfaces.action: Enlarge toolpath points for better visibility.

surfaces.label: Loop Simulation
surfaces.action: Repeat the simulation until stopped by the user.

surfaces.label: Mode
surfaces.action: Set toolpath animation mode (default: show from start until current position); down arrow opens drop-down of animation modes/functions.

surfaces.label: Show Cutting Moves
surfaces.action: Show the actual cutting (feed) movements of the tool.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Confirms the cutting moves the post emitted match the intended toolpath.

surfaces.label: Show Points
surfaces.action: Show the individual points that make up the toolpath.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Point display reveals every emitted position, letting an agent spot missing/extra/duplicate moves the post generated.

surfaces.label: Show Rapid Moves
surfaces.action: Show the rapid (non-cutting, G00) movements of the tool.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Rapid-move visualization proves the post's rapids retract to safe Z and route around stock/fixtures (pairs with Rapid To Stock stop condition).

surfaces.label: Collision (stop condition)
surfaces.action: Stop the simulation when a collision is detected.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Direct collision proof; halts at the first collision so an agent can flag the offending NC block in the post output.

surfaces.label: Stop Conditions
surfaces.action: Toggle Stop Conditions that force the simulation to stop on specific events; down arrow selects which events. Only available with Machine Simulation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Core prove-out gate: enabling stop conditions makes the simulation halt automatically on collisions, holder/stock hits, travel-limit breaches, stopped-spindle cuts, etc., turning the sim into an automatic pass/fail check on the post output.

surfaces.label: Holder To Stock (stop condition)
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Stop Conditions > Holder To Stock
surfaces.action: Stop when a collision between the tool holder and stock is detected.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Verifies the post emits enough tool stick-out / Z clearance so the holder never gouges the stock.

surfaces.label: Optional (stop condition)
surfaces.action: Stop when a program stop command is detected (M00 Program Stop, M01 Optional Stop, M02 End of Program, M30 Program End and Reset).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Confirms the post emits the correct program-control M-codes at the right points (e.g. M30 at end, M01 at optional stops).

surfaces.label: Rapid To Stock (stop condition)
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Stop Conditions > Rapid To Stock
surfaces.action: Stop when a rapid movement collides with the stock.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Catches the classic post bug of a G00 rapid plunging into stock (missing safe-Z), a key prove-out failure mode.

surfaces.label: Stopped Spindle Cuts (stop condition)
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Stop Conditions > Stopped Spindle Cuts
surfaces.action: Stop when the tool cuts while the spindle is stopped.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Proves the post emits spindle-on (M03/M04) before cutting moves; stopped-spindle cutting indicates a missing/misordered spindle command.

surfaces.label: Tool And Models (stop condition)
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Stop Conditions > Tool And Models
surfaces.action: Stop when a collision between the tool and any model (workpiece, fixture, machine) is detected.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Proves the post output never drives the tool into fixtures or machine components, the broadest collision gate.

surfaces.label: Tool Change (stop condition)
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Stop Conditions > Tool Change
surfaces.action: Stop the simulation when a tool change is detected.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent step the prove-out tool-by-tool and confirm each tool change the post emitted is valid.

surfaces.label: Travel Limits (stop condition)
surfaces.path: Backplot > Toolpath > Stop Conditions > Travel Limits
surfaces.action: Stop when an axis exceeds its travel limit.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Proves the post output keeps every axis within machine travel; halts at the first over-travel block.

surfaces.label: Toolpath
surfaces.action: Toggle visibility of toolpaths; down arrow exposes toolpath display options.

surfaces.label: Track Tool
surfaces.action: Follow the tool, keeping its position fixed on screen during simulation.

surfaces.label: Filter by used variables
surfaces.path: Backplot > docking pane > Variables tab > Filter by used variables
surfaces.action: Checkbox to show only the variables actually used within the current NC program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Narrows the variable watch to those the post output actually references, focusing the macro prove-out.

surfaces.label: Fit To Window
surfaces.action: Adjust the view to show all elements while maintaining the current perspective.

surfaces.label: Measure Distance
surfaces.action: Measure the distance between two clicked points; Fast version shows a measurement panel (left), Standard version shows measurement data in the Information Bar (bottom).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent verify dimensional correctness of a machined feature in the sim (e.g. confirm a bore diameter / depth implied by the post output) by measuring point-to-point; a sanity check on post-emitted geometry.

surfaces.label: Pan View
surfaces.action: Enable view panning by click-and-hold of the left mouse button.

surfaces.label: Perspective View
surfaces.action: Render the simulation with a camera position and field of view; camera can move through geometries for fine detail.

surfaces.label: Projection View
surfaces.action: Render the simulation preserving the relative size of geometries (orthographic-style) for comparing depths.

surfaces.label: Rotate View
surfaces.action: Enable view rotation by click-and-hold of the left mouse button.

surfaces.label: Show Axis Control
surfaces.action: Show the Axis Control panel (upper-right) tracking each axis position during simulation; any axis exceeding its travel limit is highlighted red.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Direct travel-limit verification: the panel highlights an over-travel axis in red live during the run, proving the post output keeps every axis inside machine travel.
fields: per-axis position bars (zoom via mouse wheel)

surfaces.label: Show Bounding Box
surfaces.action: Show/hide the toolpath bounding box.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Bounding box reveals the total XYZ extents of the toolpath; useful to confirm the post output stays within stock / machine envelope.

surfaces.label: Show Machine Origin
surfaces.action: Show/hide the machine origin in the simulation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Confirms the machine zero used by the post; origin placement errors are a common post bug.

surfaces.label: Show Plot Control
surfaces.action: Show/hide the plot control (playback control overlay).

surfaces.label: Show Toolpath Origin
surfaces.action: Show/hide the toolpath origin in the simulation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Confirms the work/part origin emitted by the post relative to machine zero.

surfaces.label: View from Back (XZ)
surfaces.action: View the simulation from the back (XZ plane).

surfaces.label: View from Bottom (XY)
surfaces.action: View the simulation from the bottom (XY plane).

surfaces.label: View from Front (XZ/G18)
surfaces.action: View the simulation from the front (XZ / G18 plane).

surfaces.label: View from Left (YZ/G19)
surfaces.action: View the simulation from the left (YZ / G19 plane).

surfaces.label: View from Right (YZ)
surfaces.action: View the simulation from the right (YZ plane).

surfaces.label: View from Tool
surfaces.action: Set the camera to view the simulation from the tool's perspective.

surfaces.label: View from Top (XY/G17)
surfaces.action: View the simulation from the top (XY / G17 plane).

surfaces.label: View Reset
surfaces.action: Reset the view to its initial (isometric) size and position.

surfaces.label: Zoom In
surfaces.action: Enlarge the simulation view by zooming in.

surfaces.label: Zoom Out
surfaces.action: Reduce the simulation view by zooming out.

surfaces.label: Zoom Selection
surfaces.action: Zoom in on a selected area by drawing a box (click-and-hold) around the region.

surfaces.label: Zoom To Highlighted
surfaces.action: Zoom in on the currently highlighted (active) toolpath element; requires Highlight Element enabled under Toolpath.

surfaces.label: Zoom View
surfaces.action: Enable view zoom by click-and-hold of the left mouse button (drag up to zoom in, down to zoom out).

surfaces.label: Cutter Design parameters
surfaces.action: Settable milling-cutter geometry fields (vary by cutter type): flute diameter/length, body length, shoulder diameter/length, shaft diameter, taper length, corner radius, chamfer distance.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: These dimensions are exactly what the collision/gouge engine uses; to prove a post against a golden tool you assert these match the reference tool definition.

surfaces.label: Cutter Measurement units
surfaces.path: Tool Manager > Editing cutter > Design > Measurement units
surfaces.action: Selects the unit of measurement (mm/inch) for cutter parameters.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Units-first: a cutter defined in the wrong unit is a 25.4x geometry error in the sim — this field must match the NC/post units before any geometry proving.

surfaces.label: Cutter Details tab
surfaces.action: Sets cutter metadata and STL override: Description, ID, Filename (STL model path for visual-only display), and shows Assembly number (or 'Multiple').
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The ID/Description let you key a scanned cutter back to a catalog tool when byte-comparing tool tables; the STL filename is visual-only (collision still uses configured geometry) so it is NOT a proving substitute.

surfaces.label: Editing cutter window
surfaces.action: Window to define a cutter (milling tool, turning insert, or probe — the component contacting the workpiece). Hover highlights segments; click a segment to activate its parameter field; repeat-click cycles related parameters.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Cutter geometry drives the simulation's material-removal and collision math; correct cutter definition is prerequisite to trusting any collision/limit result when proving a post.

surfaces.label: FTP Client Protocol
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [FTP machine] > Setup
surfaces.action: FTP machine configuration root with three sub-sections: Port, Send/Receive, Version Info.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Holds every parameter for shipping proven NC to a CNC over FTP. Writable as config file for blind FTP ship.

surfaces.label: Port (FTP)
surfaces.area: DNC Setup > FTP Client Protocol > Port
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [FTP] > Setup > Port
surfaces.action: Configures FTP client: server address, username, password, and default PC + FTP-server directory paths.
fields: FTP server default path (/[DIR]/ absolute from root)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the FTP target (CNC) and the local dir where proven NC sits before push. PRISM can write creds/paths to config (file) or drive the transfer via an FTP client (dnc-api) blind.

surfaces.label: Send/Receive (FTP)
surfaces.area: DNC Setup > FTP Client Protocol > Send/Receive
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [FTP] > Setup > Send/Receive
surfaces.action: Configures split-window behavior and which split-window actions are permitted (send/receive, local & remote delete/rename/dir-change/dir-create).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Permission flags gate what the FTP transfer can do; 'Send' must be allowed to push the proven NC, 'Receive to default PC directory' controls round-trip capture location for byte-compare.

surfaces.label: Version Info (FTP)
surfaces.area: DNC Setup > FTP Client Protocol > Version Info
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [FTP] > Setup > Version Info
surfaces.action: Read-only display of the FTP Client Protocol version.

surfaces.label: Standard Serial Protocol
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [serial machine] > Setup
surfaces.action: Serial machine configuration root with five sub-sections: Port, Transmit, Receive, Directories, Version Info.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Holds every parameter for a serial drip-feed of proven NC. PRISM can write these to a config file to drive a blind serial ship.

surfaces.label: Directories (serial)
surfaces.area: DNC Setup > Standard Serial Protocol > Directories
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [serial] > Setup > Directories
surfaces.action: Sets default send and receive directories plus default/additional file extensions for each.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Default send dir + extension is where PRISM drops the proven NC for the GUI to pick up; default receive dir is where round-trip captures land for byte-compare. Pure file-path config — fully writable blind.

surfaces.label: Port (serial)
surfaces.area: DNC Setup > Standard Serial Protocol > Port
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [serial] > Setup > Port
surfaces.action: Configures serial port: port, baud, stop/data bits, parity; flow control (None/Software/Hardware/Both, DTR, RTS); advanced parity/XOn/XOff handling.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Wrong baud/parity/flow corrupts the drip-feed stream; these must match the controller for a clean ship. Reading them back proves the connection is configured for the target machine.

surfaces.label: Receive (serial)
surfaces.area: DNC Setup > Standard Serial Protocol > Receive
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [serial] > Setup > Receive
surfaces.action: Configures how NC is received over serial: CR/LF (Auto/manual), line filtering/removal, start/end triggers, receive timeout, XOn-on-ready, send-at-start string.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Governs capturing a program back from the control for round-trip byte-compare; receive timeout/triggers determine clean capture of the returned NC.

surfaces.label: Transmit (serial)
surfaces.area: DNC Setup > Standard Serial Protocol > Transmit
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [serial] > Setup > Transmit
surfaces.action: Configures how NC is sent over serial: CR/LF, start/end triggers, send-at-start/end strings, line filtering/cleanup, pacing, handshake timeout, manual-start gate.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Directly governs the drip-feed: triggers/CR-LF/whitespace handling alter the bytes the machine receives. To prove a post, these must NOT mangle the verified NC (or must be set to pass it through verbatim) — byte-compare sent stream vs golden depends on these.

surfaces.label: Version Info (serial)
surfaces.area: DNC Setup > Standard Serial Protocol > Version Info
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > [serial] > Setup > Version Info
surfaces.action: Read-only display of the Standard Serial Protocol version.

surfaces.label: DNC Setup (dialog)
surfaces.action: Root config dialog for all machine configurations: lists machines, sets protocol (serial/FTP), shows port shorthand, machine type, and Setup/Rename/Add New/Delete/OK actions. Persists to the DNC machine-config store.
fields: Protocol (Standard Serial Protocol | FTP Client Protocol)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the connection used to ship proven NC. PRISM could write this config file directly (port/baud/protocol/dirs) to set up a target machine without the GUI before a drip-feed.

surfaces.label: Add New (machine)
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > Add New
surfaces.action: Adds a new machine configuration. Prompts for a name and a template to preconfigure from.
fields: Template (FTP Client | Generic Serial Connected CNC | Okuma Template | existing machine config)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Creates the target-machine config that a proven post will be shipped to; templates (Okuma/Generic Serial/FTP) bootstrap the connection. Writable as config file by PRISM.

surfaces.label: Delete (machine)
surfaces.action: Deletes the selected machine configuration (confirmation prompt).

surfaces.label: Machine Type
surfaces.path: Transmission > Setup > DNC Setup > Machine Type
surfaces.action: Selects machine type, which determines default load/save directories and tool-change detection during transfer. Types are configured in File Types in Editor Setup.
fields: Machine Type (list, sourced from Editor Setup > File Types)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Machine type drives default send/receive dirs + tool-change detection on the streamed NC — relevant when proving the post's tool-change syntax is recognized correctly.

surfaces.label: Protocol
surfaces.action: Per-machine dropdown to select communication protocol: Standard Serial Protocol (serial) or FTP Client Protocol (FTP).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Determines whether the ship goes over serial drip-feed or FTP push; must match the real machine for the proven NC to land.

surfaces.label: Rename (machine)
surfaces.action: Renames the selected machine configuration.

surfaces.label: Setup (machine config)
surfaces.action: Opens the per-machine configuration dialog (Port/Transmit/Receive/Directories/Version Info for serial, or Port/Send-Receive/Version Info for FTP).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Entry to the detailed port + transmit settings that govern how the proven NC is streamed (baud, handshake, triggers, delays).

surfaces.label: Add Bookmark / Remove Bookmark
surfaces.action: Creates a named bookmark on the selected line via the Add Bookmark dialog; toggles to Remove Bookmark if the line is already bookmarked.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Mark a specific NC line of interest (e.g. a suspect block) for later jump during proof review.

surfaces.label: Go to Next
surfaces.action: Jumps to the next bookmark in the document.

surfaces.label: Go to Previous
surfaces.action: Jumps to the previous bookmark in the document.

surfaces.label: Toggle Indicators
surfaces.action: Toggles display of bookmark indicators (line-number highlights; requires Show line numbers enabled).

surfaces.label: View Bookmarks
surfaces.action: Opens the Bookmarks dialog showing all bookmarks across all open (saved) documents, with buttons to delete, clear, or jump to a bookmarked location.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: After Bookmark-All from a Find, the bookmark list enumerates every flagged NC location for systematic inspection. Note: only shows for saved documents.

surfaces.label: Append File
surfaces.action: Appends an external file to the end of the current CNC program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Concatenate sub-programs/tool sections into one NC stream for a full-program proof; directly achievable by file concatenation off-GUI.

surfaces.label: Copy
surfaces.action: Copies the selected text to the clipboard.

surfaces.label: Cut
surfaces.action: Deletes the selected text and saves it to the clipboard for pasting elsewhere.

surfaces.label: Insert File
surfaces.action: Inserts an external file into the current window at the cursor position.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Splice a header/footer or subprogram into the NC at a point; achievable directly by file edit off-GUI.

surfaces.label: Mark/Delete range
surfaces.action: Opens the Mark/Delete dialog to select/update/delete a range of lines or block numbers, including special selection/deletion from a tool change, feed rate or spindle speed value up to the next one. Also reachable from Insert/Remove on the NC Functions tab.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Isolating a tool-change or feed/speed range lets an agent extract the exact NC segment around an event to verify a post emitted it correctly.
fields: Selection from tool change to next
Selection from feed rate to next
Selection from spindle speed to next

surfaces.label: Paste
surfaces.action: Inserts the clipboard contents at the current cursor position.

surfaces.label: Redo
surfaces.action: Redoes the last undone operation; can redo all undos since the file was last opened.

surfaces.label: Select All
surfaces.action: Selects all lines in the file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Select-all then copy is a blind way to extract the entire NC buffer text via the clipboard for byte-compare against a golden file.

surfaces.label: Undo
surfaces.action: Undoes the last operation.

surfaces.label: Advanced Open
surfaces.action: Locates files by search criteria on file name, file content, and created/modified dates via the Advanced Open dialog (under the Open icon down-arrow).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Could find a specific candidate NC file by content signature when proving a batch, but for a known path direct file-open is simpler.

surfaces.label: Close
surfaces.action: Closes the current window; prompts to save if the file was modified.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Teardown between proof iterations; the save prompt is a modal an agent must handle/dismiss.

surfaces.label: Close All
surfaces.action: Closes all open windows; prompts to save for each modified file (under the Close icon down-arrow).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Bulk teardown after a multi-file proof batch.

surfaces.label: Global setup
surfaces.action: Opens the general program settings of CIMCO Edit (Editor Settings); also reachable through the gear/settings icon.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Editor Settings hold file-type/backplot/tool-change-identification config that governs how an NC program is parsed and simulated when proving a post.

surfaces.label: New
surfaces.action: Creates an empty program/file ready for input.

surfaces.label: Open
surfaces.action: Opens a file via the standard Open file dialog.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Primary way to load a generated NC program into the editor for inspection; blind agents prefer launching the exe with the file path as a CLI arg to bypass the GUI dialog.

surfaces.label: Print
surfaces.action: Prints the current CNC program; if a region is marked, prints only that selection.

surfaces.label: Printer Setup
surfaces.action: Opens the printout configuration dialog (under the Print icon down-arrow). See the Printing section for details.

surfaces.label: Recent
surfaces.action: Lists recently used files for quick reopening (under the Open icon down-arrow).

surfaces.label: Save
surfaces.action: Saves the current CNC program under its current name.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Persists any edits made during proof; for blind operation the .nc file can be read/written directly off disk instead.

surfaces.label: Save All
surfaces.action: Saves all open CNC programs under their current names (under the Save icon down-arrow).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Persists a whole batch of proof files at once.

surfaces.label: Save As
surfaces.action: Saves the current CNC program under a new name via a Save As dialog.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Write the proven/edited NC out to a golden-output path for later byte-compare.

surfaces.label: Save as associated file
surfaces.path: Editor > File > Save as associated file
surfaces.action: Saves the current CNC program into CIMCO NC-Base, prompting for Machine, Program Name and filename, then associates it with the selected NC-Base program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Links a proven program to a machine record in the NC-Base datastore — useful for round-tripping proven NC into the DNC/NC-Base catalog.

surfaces.label: Block Numbering
surfaces.action: Opens the Block Numbers dialog in Editor Setup for the selected file type to configure block (N-number) renumbering.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Block-numbering config governs how N-numbers are emitted/renumbered; matters when byte-comparing generated NC to a golden file that has specific N-numbering.

surfaces.label: Colors
surfaces.action: Opens the Color Settings page of Editor Setup for the selected file type to define syntax color highlighting.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Cosmetic; underlying file-type config is editable on disk so this dialog can be skipped for blind operation.

surfaces.label: Load/Save (Directories and Extensions)
surfaces.action: Opens the Load/Save dialog in Editor Setup for the selected file type to configure default directories and file extensions.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines where files of a type load/save and which extensions map to the type — sets the path/extension contract a blind agent uses to locate generated NC.

surfaces.label: Machine Templates
surfaces.action: Opens the Machine dialog in Editor Setup for the selected file type to configure machine-template-specific parameters.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Machine-template parameters (axis/limit/feed conventions used by backplot and parsing) are central to proving a post against the correct machine; config is file-backed.

surfaces.label: Other Settings
surfaces.action: Opens the Other dialog in Editor Setup for the selected file type to configure additional machine settings.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Holds additional machine settings that affect parsing/backplot of the program under proof; file-backed.

surfaces.label: File Type (dropdown)
surfaces.action: Dropdown to select the active file type, which determines coloring, syntax, renumbering, tool-change identification, etc.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The file type controls how the editor parses tool changes / feed / speed and how backplot interprets the program — picking the right one is a prerequisite for accurate proving. Underlying config maps to a CIMCO .mcfg-style file readable/writable directly.

surfaces.label: Setup File Type
surfaces.path: Editor > File Type > Setup File Type
surfaces.action: Opens the File Types dialog in Editor Setup to add new or configure existing file types.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Registers a new machine/post file type with its tool-change/feed/speed identification rules — the master config that makes the editor and backplot understand a given post's output. Editable as a CIMCO config file.

surfaces.label: Find
surfaces.action: Opens the Find/Search dialog to search the current (or all open) files; supports plain text, whole-string, case, regex, NC-command search, and bookmark/find-all bulk actions.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Searching for G/M codes, tool numbers, feed/speed words or alarm strings is how an agent verifies a post emitted (or omitted) specific commands; regex + Find All gives every occurrence for assertion.
fields: Find NC Command (Tool Change / Feedrate / Spindle Speed dropdown)

surfaces.label: Find All (results dialog)
surfaces.action: Shows an overview dialog of all matching search results; clicking a result selects it in the file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Enumerates every occurrence of an NC token at once — an agent can count/assert all matches (e.g. exactly N tool changes) when proving a post.

surfaces.label: Find Next
surfaces.action: Finds the next occurrence of the specified search string in the file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Step forward through matches of an NC command/value while verifying program structure.

surfaces.label: Find Previous
surfaces.action: Finds the previous occurrence of the specified search string in the file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Step backward through matches of an NC command/value while verifying program structure.

surfaces.label: Go to Line/Block Number
surfaces.path: Editor > Find > Go to Line/Block Number
surfaces.action: Moves the cursor to a specified line or block number in the current file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Jump to a known line/block to read the NC at a reported error/collision location.

surfaces.label: Next Tool Change
surfaces.action: Moves the cursor to the next tool change in the program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Step through tool changes to verify the post emitted correct tool-call/length-offset blocks per operation.

surfaces.label: Previous Tool Change
surfaces.action: Moves the cursor to the previous tool change in the program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Step backward through tool changes to verify post output around each tool.

surfaces.label: Replace
surfaces.action: Opens the Replace dialog to replace a string with another; supports selection-only, whole-string, regex, multiline, result-to-new-window, and bulk Replace-All-from-File with a delimiter.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Normalizing variable fields (dates, comments, tool comments) before a byte-compare vs golden; Replace-All-from-File can apply a known find/replace map to the generated NC.

surfaces.label: Replace All from File
surfaces.path: Editor > Find > Replace > Replace All from File
surfaces.action: Imports one or more find/replace pairs from an external delimited file (e.g. T1;T10) and applies them all at once after choosing the file and delimiter.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Batch-normalize many tokens (tool renames, address swaps) in generated NC from a prepared mapping file before comparing to a golden reference.

surfaces.label: Editor
surfaces.action: Top-level Ribbon tab grouping the core text-editing command groups (File, File Type, Edit, Find, Bookmarks, Setup, Window, Help).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Entry tab an agent must activate first to reach Open/Save/Find for loading and inspecting an NC program under proof.

surfaces.label: Backplot
surfaces.action: Top-level Ribbon tab for graphical toolpath backplot/simulation — sibling tab, not detailed on these pages.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Backplot is the simulation surface for proving a post — load NC, render toolpath, read limits/collisions. Detailed in other clusters.

surfaces.label: File Compare
surfaces.action: Top-level Ribbon tab for side-by-side NC file comparison — sibling tab, not detailed on these pages.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: File Compare is the byte/line-diff surface for comparing generated NC against a golden reference. Detailed in other clusters.

surfaces.label: NC-Assistant
surfaces.action: Top-level Ribbon tab for the NC-Assistant context help feature — sibling tab, not detailed on these pages.

surfaces.label: NC Functions
surfaces.action: Top-level Ribbon tab for NC-program editing functions (renumber, insert/remove, etc.) — sibling tab, not detailed on these pages.

surfaces.label: Transmission
surfaces.action: Top-level Ribbon tab for serial/DNC transmission of programs to/from machines — sibling tab, not detailed on these pages.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Transmission is the drip-feed/send surface for delivering verified NC to a machine. Best driven via DNC-Max API. Detailed in other clusters.

surfaces.label: Close Left Window
surfaces.path: File Compare > File Compare > Close Left Window
surfaces.action: Closes the file-compare window on the left side.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Housekeeping after a diff; lets an agent discard the left (e.g. golden) pane while keeping the candidate open.

surfaces.label: Close Right Window
surfaces.path: File Compare > File Compare > Close Right Window
surfaces.action: Closes the file-compare window on the right side.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Housekeeping after a diff; lets an agent discard the right (e.g. candidate) pane while keeping the golden open.

surfaces.label: Compare File with File
surfaces.path: File Compare > File Compare > Compare File with File
surfaces.action: Compares two files that are not already open, both opened through the Open file dialog.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Primary GUI golden byte-diff entry: select candidate NC + golden NC from disk and diff in-app, honoring the Ignore Options (block numbers/whitespace/comments/case/numeric format). For an exact byte-compare PRISM should diff on the file channel; use this only when CIMCO's NC-aware ignore semantics are wanted.

surfaces.label: Compare with File
surfaces.path: File Compare > File Compare > Compare with File
surfaces.action: Compares the file in the current window against a file picked via the Open file dialog.
fields: other file (chosen via Open file dialog)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Diffs the current/just-posted NC against a golden file on disk selected through the Open dialog. Good for proving a post when the candidate is already loaded; the file-picker step is a UIA dialog an agent must drive blind.

surfaces.label: Compare with Window
surfaces.path: File Compare > File Compare > Compare with Window
surfaces.action: Compares the file in the current window with a file in another open window. With >2 files open, CIMCO prompts which file to compare against.
fields: target window (prompted when more than two files are open)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Diffs a freshly-posted NC already open in a window against another already-open window (e.g. golden reference loaded in a second tab). Useful when both NC outputs are loaded in-app, but the prompt-on-3+-files makes it brittle to drive blind — prefer Compare File with File.

surfaces.label: End File Compare
surfaces.path: File Compare > File Compare > End File Compare
surfaces.action: Stops the file-compare session; both files are left open.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Teardown step after a golden-diff run so the editor returns to a normal state before the next post-proving cycle.

surfaces.label: Setup
surfaces.action: Opens the File Compare section of the Editor Setup dialog.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Gateway to the ignore/marking settings that govern whether a golden diff treats block-number/whitespace/comment/case/numeric variation as a difference — must be configured correctly before trusting an in-app post-prove diff.

surfaces.label: Go to First Difference
surfaces.path: File Compare > Go To > Go to First Difference
surfaces.action: Jumps to the first difference in the compare.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Resets the diff cursor to the top so a post-proving sweep starts from a known position.

surfaces.label: Go to Last Difference
surfaces.path: File Compare > Go To > Go to Last Difference
surfaces.action: Jumps to the last difference in the compare.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Jumps the diff cursor to the bottom; with First Difference brackets the diff range so an agent can bound how many differences a candidate post has vs golden.

surfaces.label: Next Difference
surfaces.path: File Compare > Go To > Next Difference
surfaces.action: Steps to the next difference found during the compare.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent walk every diff between candidate and golden NC to enumerate/inspect each discrepancy during post-proving. The Ctrl+Down shortcut makes it scriptable blind via keystroke injection.

surfaces.label: Previous Difference
surfaces.path: File Compare > Go To > Previous Difference
surfaces.action: Steps to the previous difference found during the compare.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Reverse-direction diff walk; pairs with Next Difference to navigate the diff set when inspecting candidate-vs-golden NC. Ctrl+Up makes it blind-drivable.

surfaces.label: File Compare Setup
surfaces.path: File Compare > Other > File Compare Setup
surfaces.action: Opens the File Compare section of the Editor Setup dialog (duplicate gateway to the same setup screen as File Compare menu > Setup).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Second route to the ignore/marking config that determines whether an in-app golden diff treats NC formatting variation as a difference.

surfaces.label: Save Compare File
surfaces.path: File Compare > Other > Save Compare File
surfaces.action: Saves the lines that differ between the two files to a .txt file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: HIGH — the only documented way to externalize CIMCO's diff result. After Compare File with File, this writes a .txt of differing lines that PRISM can then read on the file channel to assert zero (or expected) deltas vs golden NC. The export bridges the GUI diff to a machine-readable artifact.

surfaces.label: Single Step Through Differences
surfaces.path: File Compare > Other > Single Step Through Differences
surfaces.action: Toggle: when enabled, only the line at the cursor is synchronized (one line at a time) instead of CIMCO's default block-of-lines sync.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Controls diff-walk granularity (per-line vs per-block). Affects how finely an agent can inspect/step diffs; mirrors the 'Single line step' setup checkbox.

surfaces.label: File Compare (Editor Setup)
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare
surfaces.action: Per-File-Type configuration dialog for compare behaviour (settings, ignore options, print options). Settings apply only to the selected File Type, shown at the top of the dialog; persisted in the editor/file-type config (.mcfg).
fields: File Type (selected at top; change via File Types section)
Jump to next difference after sync.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: HIGH — governs the semantics of every golden diff. For NC post-proving the Ignore Options are decisive: Ignore Block numbers, Ignore White spaces, Ignore Comments, Ignore Case, Ignore Numeric format let a diff pass on cosmetic-only variation OR be made strict for an exact byte-prove. Because settings persist in the file-type config, PRISM can pre-set them on the file channel (.mcfg) before driving CIMCO, instead of clicking checkboxes blind.

surfaces.label: Ignore Block numbers
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > Ignore Options
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Ignore Options > Ignore Block numbers
surfaces.action: Checkbox — ignore block-number values and their presence/absence (N-word differences and one file having N-numbers while the other does not are ignored).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: HIGH — block (N) numbering commonly differs between a renumbered candidate post and golden. Enable to prove geometry/command equivalence while ignoring N renumbering; DISABLE for a strict byte-exact prove that includes N-words.

surfaces.label: Ignore Case
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > Ignore Options
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Ignore Options > Ignore Case
surfaces.action: Checkbox — ignore letter case (lowercase vs UPPERCASE for the same command treated as equal).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Moderate for NC — most controllers expect uppercase; enable only if comparing a post that emits mixed case against a golden, otherwise keep DISABLED so a case discrepancy that would matter to the controller is flagged.

surfaces.label: Ignore Comments
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > Ignore Options
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Ignore Options > Ignore Comments
surfaces.action: Checkbox — ignore anything inside a comment; requires the Comment start (e.g. '(') and Comment end (e.g. ')') to be set in the Machine Template for the selected file type.
fields: depends on Machine Template Comment start/end characters
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: HIGH — posts frequently emit timestamped/operator/date comments that differ run-to-run. Enable to prove the executable NC matches golden while ignoring comment churn; DISABLE if proving comment content too. Note the dependency on Machine Template comment chars (setupmachine.htm).

surfaces.label: Ignore Numeric format
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > Ignore Options
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Ignore Options > Ignore Numeric format
surfaces.action: Checkbox — ignore leading/trailing zeros and optional '+' characters (e.g. 'X+14.10' matches 'X14.1').
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: HIGH — numeric formatting (leading/trailing zeros, explicit '+') is exactly the kind of post-processor formatting that legitimately varies. Enable to prove numeric equivalence of coordinates; DISABLE for an exact-format prove where the controller's number format (e.g. trailing-zero suppression) is part of what the post must get right.

surfaces.label: Ignore White spaces
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > Ignore Options
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Ignore Options > Ignore White spaces
surfaces.action: Checkbox — ignore white-space characters: space (ASCII 32) and tab (ASCII 9).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: HIGH for NC golden-diff — spacing between words often varies post-to-post. Enable to prove token equivalence; DISABLE for an exact byte prove where spacing/format must match golden verbatim.

surfaces.label: Jump to next difference after sync.
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > File Compare Settings
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Jump to next difference after sync.
surfaces.action: Checkbox — always jump to the next difference after synchronizing two differences.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Workflow convenience for sync-driven reconciliation; minor for a read-only golden-prove (sync is a mutation path).

surfaces.label: Mark Changes only
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > File Compare Settings
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Mark Changes only
surfaces.action: Checkbox — activate all lines with at least one difference but highlight only the differing portion, not the entire line.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Highlight granularity (changed-chars vs whole-line). Helps an agent localize the exact differing tokens in an NC line during post-proving.

surfaces.label: Print only differences
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > Print Options
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Print Options > Print only differences
surfaces.action: Checkbox — when printing, print only the lines that differ between the two files.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Print-side analog of Save Compare File; low automation value since printing is not machine-readable. For a post-prove artifact prefer Save Compare File (.txt) over print.

surfaces.label: Show all differences (No editing)
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > File Compare Settings
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Show all differences (No editing)
surfaces.action: Checkbox — show all lines with at least one difference, highlighting every difference simultaneously; read-only (no editing).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Read-only all-at-once diff view — ideal for a non-mutating golden-prove pass where the agent only needs to confirm the full set of NC differences without risk of editing either file.

surfaces.label: Single line step
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > File Compare Settings
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Single line step
surfaces.action: Checkbox — single-step through multiple consecutive differences; only the difference on the current line is highlighted.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Diff-walk granularity setting (per-line). Determines how an agent steps candidate-vs-golden differences during inspection.

surfaces.label: Use smart marking
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > File Compare Settings
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Use smart marking
surfaces.action: Checkbox — mark not just the differing part but the complete command if it contains at least one difference.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Marks whole NC commands (e.g. a full G/M block) when any sub-token differs — useful when proving that a post emits the correct full command, not just a stray character.

surfaces.label: Use tab to switch window
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Compare > File Compare Settings
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > File Compare > Use tab to switch window
surfaces.action: Checkbox — use the Tab key to switch between the two compared files; while enabled, Tab cannot be inserted into either file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Navigation key remap between panes; affects how an agent moves focus blind during a diff but does not change diff results.

surfaces.label: Sync Left
surfaces.action: Synchronizes the current difference from the right window to the left window (copies the diff right-to-left; the line de-highlights once both sides match).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Mutation, not verification — copies content between panes. Generally NOT used in a read-only golden-prove (it would alter a file); relevant only if an agent is reconciling a candidate toward golden. Flag as edit-capable.

surfaces.label: Sync Right
surfaces.action: Synchronizes the current difference from the left window to the right window (copies the diff left-to-right; the line de-highlights once both sides match).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Mutation, not verification — copies content between panes. NOT used in a read-only golden-prove; relevant only when reconciling files. Flag as edit-capable.

surfaces.label: File Compare
surfaces.action: Top-level ribbon tab that hosts the four file-compare command groups (File Compare, Go To, Sync, Other). Container only.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Entry point for the entire GUI golden-diff arm: an agent must activate this tab to reach Compare File with File and Save Compare File. To prove a post, the byte-compare itself is better done off-GUI (file channel), but this tab is the only documented in-app diff surface.

surfaces.label: FTP Transfer Dialog (Split Window)
surfaces.action: Dual-pane FTP client: local PC (left) vs remote CNC FTP server (right). Send/receive files and manage directories between them.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The FTP SHIP surface: 'Arrow right' pushes the proven NC file to the CNC; 'Arrow left' pulls it back for byte-compare. PRISM can replicate this entirely via an FTP client (dnc-api) against the same server/creds — full blind ship without the GUI.

surfaces.label: Delete (FTP file/folder)
surfaces.action: Deletes selected file/folder on local or remote side (requires Local/Remote deletion enabled).

surfaces.label: File type dropdown (PC side)
surfaces.path: Transmission > FTP Transfer Dialog > File type
