surfaces.action: Specifies the file type/filter used when sending programs from the PC side.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Selecting the NC file type ensures the proven program is the one offered for FTP push.

surfaces.label: New folder
surfaces.path: Transmission > FTP Transfer Dialog > New folder
surfaces.action: Creates a new folder on local or remote side (requires Local/Remote directory creation enabled in Send/Receive setup).

surfaces.label: Arrow pointing left (Receive)
surfaces.path: Transmission > FTP Transfer Dialog > Arrow left
surfaces.action: Receives selected file(s) from the remote FTP server (CNC) to the local PC.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Pulls the NC back from the control for round-trip integrity byte-compare against the golden post output.

surfaces.label: Refresh
surfaces.action: Refreshes both local and remote directory listings.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Confirms the pushed NC actually landed on the remote (it appears in the remote listing after refresh) — a ship-confirmation read.

surfaces.label: Rename (FTP file/folder)
surfaces.action: Renames selected file/folder on local or remote side (requires Local/Remote renaming enabled).

surfaces.label: Arrow pointing right (Send)
surfaces.path: Transmission > FTP Transfer Dialog > Arrow right
surfaces.action: Sends selected file(s) from local PC to the remote FTP server (CNC).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The literal push of proven NC onto the machine over FTP — the FTP equivalent of the drip-feed ship. Replicable blind via FTP PUT.

surfaces.label: Holder Design tab (Milling)
surfaces.action: Defines a milling holder as a stack of segments. Controls: Measurement units, Add New Holder Segment, Delete all Holder Segments; per-segment Upper/Lower/Length, up/down reorder arrows, and close-icon to remove.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The segment stack is the swept profile used for holder-collision detection during sim — building it correctly is required before clearance results can prove the post's retract/Z-clearance moves are safe.

surfaces.label: Holder Design tab (Turning/Lathe)
surfaces.action: Defines a turning/lathe holder via type-specific parameter fields; selecting a parameter highlights the corresponding holder region in the preview.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lathe holder geometry/orientation governs turret-clearance and back-of-tool collision checks when proving a lathe post.

surfaces.label: Holder Details tab
surfaces.action: Sets holder metadata and STL override: Description, ID, Filename (visual-only STL path), and shows Assembly number (or 'Multiple').
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: STL filename is visual-only (collision uses configured holder geometry), so it cannot substitute for a correct holder definition when proving clearances.

surfaces.label: Editing holder window
surfaces.action: Window to define a holder (milling = sequence of segments; turning = type-specific params). Hover highlights segment, click activates parameter field, repeat-click cycles parameters.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Holder geometry is the body the sim checks for holder-vs-stock and holder-vs-fixture collisions; an undersized/missing holder hides real collisions when proving a post.

surfaces.label: Find Macro
surfaces.action: Searches the open NC program for the macro selected in the Macro Name dropdown (or via Cycles/Macros field + Find Macro button); errors 'Cannot find the macro ...' if the block was not recognized as a macro (e.g. manually copied/created text).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: A pass/fail recognition probe: if Find Macro locates the expected cycle in a post-generated NC file, the block conforms to the macro pattern; 'Cannot find' flags a malformed/non-conforming post output.

surfaces.label: Formulas sample file
surfaces.action: Predefined sample formula macros demonstrating formula usage; selectable via the Formulas File Type. Source file at <CIMCO Edit dir>\Samples\Formulas\formulas.MAC.

surfaces.label: Formula syntax / math functions
surfaces.action: Formulas written @N{...} (like $N variables, same formatting). Operators + - * / % and nested ( ); functions abs, acos, asin, atan, cos, cosh, floor, ln, log, sign, sin, sinh, sqrt, tan, tanh; PI constant; angles in degrees; trig args must use parentheses e.g. sin($1). One-line macro can output only the formula result.
fields: functions: abs acos asin atan cos cosh floor ln log sign sin sinh sqrt tan tanh
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the deterministic value-derivation rules; an agent can recompute a formula in the .MAC and assert the post-emitted derived value (e.g. computed radius/area/coordinate) matches expected output.

surfaces.label: Hide Balloons
surfaces.action: Toggles the yellow hover balloon (tooltip) that shows an easy-to-read overview of NC code parameters when hovering over a code.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: When balloons are on, hovering a line in a post-generated file surfaces the parsed parameter breakdown via UIA tooltip text — a non-screenshot way to read how CIMCO interprets each NC code.

surfaces.label: Hide Sidebar
surfaces.action: Toggles visibility of the NC-Assistant sidebar (macro list / parameter editor).

surfaces.label: Insert Macro
surfaces.action: Inserts the macro selected in the Macros menu Macro Name dropdown at the cursor; opens an Insert dialog whose parameter fields vary by macro (required + optional* params), OK to insert.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent inject a known-good canonical NC block (e.g. drilling cycle, program start/end) to compare against post-generated output; the Insert dialog surfaces the parameterization the post must reproduce.

surfaces.label: Macro Setup
surfaces.action: Opens the Macro Setup dialog to configure/add/modify macros for different file types.

surfaces.label: Add
surfaces.action: Button: opens Add macro dialog to name and create a new macro (inserted right after the selected macro in the list).

surfaces.label: Add Formula
surfaces.action: Button: inserts a new formula '@N{...}' (e.g. @3{sqrt($1*$1 + $2*$2)}) into the macro definition.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Formulas compute output values from inputs; verifying the inserted formula result matches an expected computed value is a numeric correctness check on derived NC parameters.

surfaces.label: Add Info
surfaces.action: Button: inserts the System variable selected in the Info variable dropdown into the macro definition.

surfaces.label: Add User Input
surfaces.action: Button: inserts a new User variable ($1, $2, $3, ...) into the macro definition.

surfaces.label: Copy
surfaces.action: Button: makes a copy of the selected macro (edit name/contents to derive a similar macro).

surfaces.label: Copy Group
surfaces.action: Button: opens Copy Macro Groups dialog to copy macro groups from one File Type to others; Duplicate Copy Behavior dropdown handles collisions.
fields: Duplicate Copy Behavior (Skip duplicates / Overwrite duplicates / Abort copy of duplicate)

surfaces.label: Copy To
surfaces.action: Button: opens Copy Macros dialog to copy one or more selected macros (checkboxes) to a target Machine Type and Macro Group.

surfaces.label: Macro definition field
surfaces.action: Large text field holding the macro body: text, user variables ($1..), system variables ($UPPERNAME), formulas (@N{...}), block numbers (# / ## literal), char-after-variable ('|'), leading blank line forces new line. Persists in the .MAC file.
fields: leading blank line = start on new line
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the exact text template a post block must match; readable/writable via the .MAC file so an agent can byte-compare post output against the macro's literal+parameterized form.

surfaces.label: Delete
surfaces.action: Button: deletes the selected macro after a Yes/No confirmation.

surfaces.label: Macro Setup Dialog
surfaces.action: Three-area dialog (macro list / macro definition / parameter config) to configure, add and modify macros per file type. Macros persist to .MAC files at %appdata%\CIMCO 2026\CIMCOEdit\Types\ — editable directly without the GUI.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The .MAC files are the file-channel hook: an agent can author/inspect macro definitions (canonical block templates + parameter rules) programmatically, then drive Insert/Find in the GUI to validate post output against them.

surfaces.label: Favorite
surfaces.action: Button: favorites/un-favorites a macro; favorites appear in the Favorites group formatted {group}->{macro}.

surfaces.label: Info variable
surfaces.action: Dropdown listing available System variables (date, time, date+time, filename, etc.) for insertion into the macro body.
fields: system variable dropdown (date, time, datetime, filename, ...)

surfaces.label: Macro .MAC config files
surfaces.action: Per-file-type .MAC files storing all macro group/name definitions, bodies, variables, formulas and parameter rules. Import/backup by copying these files; editable without the GUI.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The primary blind/file-channel surface: PRISM can parse the .MAC corpus to obtain canonical block templates + formatting rules per controller, then byte/pattern-compare them against post-generated NC without touching the GUI.

surfaces.label: Machine Type
surfaces.action: Dropdown of defined machine types (e.g. ISO Milling, ISO Turning, Heidenhain); changing it updates the Macro group dropdown with that type's groups.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Selects the controller dialect whose macros define the expected NC block shapes for that post — sets the verification baseline.

surfaces.label: Macro group
surfaces.action: Dropdown of defined macro groups; Edit Macro Groups icon opens a dialog to create/rename/delete groups.

surfaces.label: Macro name
surfaces.action: Listbox of all macros for the selected machine type and macro group.

surfaces.label: Move To
surfaces.action: Button: moves selected macros to a different Machine Type/Macro Group (like Copy To but deletes from the source).

surfaces.label: Allow letters
surfaces.action: Checkbox: allow text-string input; auto-wraps text in parentheses per ISO; grays out Min/Max/Decimals/Digits/Allow negative.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Auto-parenthesizing of comment text matches ISO comment convention a post must emit — verifiable against comment formatting in post output.

surfaces.label: Allow negative values
surfaces.action: Checkbox: allows negative values; if unchecked a negative input has its sign ignored (absolute value used).

surfaces.label: Hide formula results (in entire macro)
surfaces.path: Macro Setup > (param) Hide formula results (in entire macro)
surfaces.action: Checkbox: hide NC-Assistant macro formula results for this macro (overridden by the global Editor Setup option if that is set).

surfaces.label: Insert with sign
surfaces.action: Checkbox: inserts the value with an explicit sign (123.4 -> +123.4).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Explicit-plus-sign formatting is a controller-specific post option; verifiable against post output.

surfaces.label: Do not insert empty lines
surfaces.path: Macro Setup > (param) Do not insert empty lines
surfaces.action: Checkbox: suppress a blank line when this parameter is not specified.

surfaces.label: Remember value
surfaces.action: Checkbox: reuse the last entered value for this parameter on the next macro call (e.g. keep X,Y/feed while varying Z depth).

surfaces.label: Parameter is required
surfaces.action: Checkbox: marks the parameter as required; if unchecked the field shows * (optional/modal, e.g. X,Y,Z on G01).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Required vs optional/modal addressing mirrors how a post should (or should not) re-emit modal words — useful for verifying modal-suppression behavior in post output.

surfaces.label: Uppercase
surfaces.action: Checkbox: force user text input to uppercase (only meaningful when Allow letters is enabled).

surfaces.label: Macro attachment
surfaces.action: Field + Select attachment / Clear attachment buttons: attach a file (e.g. help doc) opened via a button in the Insert dialog.

surfaces.label: Decimals
surfaces.action: Dropdown: number of decimal digits — As specified / Any (>=1 decimal) / 0-5 fixed.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Decimal-format control directly governs the numeric formatting a post must reproduce; a mismatch is a classic post defect (e.g. 10.0 vs 10.000).

surfaces.label: Default value
surfaces.action: Text field: default value for the selected parameter (restorable via the Default button in Modify Macro).

surfaces.label: Description
surfaces.action: Text field: description of the selected parameter, shown next to the field in the Insert dialog.

surfaces.label: Digits
surfaces.action: Dropdown: number of integer digits / zero-padding (e.g. 4-digit O-number outputs O0007).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Zero-padding/digit-width control for program numbers and addresses — verifiable against post output formatting (e.g. O-number width).

surfaces.label: Macro illustration / Parameter illustration
surfaces.action: Field + Select Picture / No Picture buttons: attach a general macro image or a per-parameter image shown in the Insert dialog.

surfaces.label: Max
surfaces.action: Text field: maximum allowed value; entering higher prompts immediate correction.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Upper limit bound for a parameter; supports limit/overrun checks on post-emitted values.

surfaces.label: Min
surfaces.action: Text field: minimum allowed value; entering lower prompts immediate correction.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Per-parameter limit bound; analogous to machine-axis/feed limits — an agent can use Min/Max to flag post values outside the safe envelope.

surfaces.label: Predefined values
surfaces.action: Checkbox + Configure choices button: restrict the parameter to a list of Label/Inserted value pairs presented as a dropdown in the Insert dialog.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the enumerated set of legal values (e.g. canned-cycle codes); a post emitting a value outside this set is non-conforming.

surfaces.label: Prefix
surfaces.action: Text field: prefix string added before the parameter value (e.g. T for tool, S for spindle speed).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the address letter the post must emit before a value (T/S/F/G); verifiable against post output.

surfaces.label: Suffix
surfaces.action: Text field: suffix string added after the parameter value.

surfaces.label: Rename
surfaces.action: Button: renames the selected macro.

surfaces.label: Up / Down arrows
surfaces.action: Buttons: move the selected macro up/down the list (larger arrows move 10 places).

surfaces.label: User Input Order
surfaces.action: Button: opens a dialog with up/down arrows to reorder how User variables are presented in the Insert dialog (does not change order in the inserted NC text).

surfaces.label: File Type
surfaces.action: Dropdown showing/selecting the current file type; mirrors the File Type dropdown in the Editor tab. Determines which macro set (machine dialect) applies.
fields: file type dropdown (e.g. ISO Milling, ISO Turning, Heidenhain, Formulas)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Selecting the correct File Type aligns CIMCO's parser with the target controller dialect — prerequisite for any macro-based recognition check of post output to be meaningful.

surfaces.label: Macro Group
surfaces.action: Dropdown showing/selecting the current Macro Group (groups configured in Macro Setup dialog).

surfaces.label: Macro Name
surfaces.action: Dropdown showing/selecting the currently active macro; this selection is what Insert Macro and Find Macro operate on.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Drives which canonical block Insert/Find target — the agent sets this to the cycle it wants to verify in a post-generated file.

surfaces.label: Modify Macro
surfaces.action: Modifies the macro at the cursor position; place cursor on macro-code (ribbon icon activates) then opens Modify dialog to update parameter values; Default button reverts to defined defaults; OK applies.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Reading the Modify dialog confirms CIMCO can re-parse a post-emitted block back into its macro parameters — a round-trip recognition check that the block is well-formed per the machine type.

surfaces.label: Close
surfaces.action: Closes the Multi Channel view.

surfaces.label: Files
surfaces.action: Views multiple files together in Multi Channel mode.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Loads separate per-channel NC files side-by-side to verify cross-channel Wait-code synchronization of post output when channels are emitted as distinct files.

surfaces.label: Next
surfaces.action: Jumps to the next synchronization point (Wait code) in Multi Channel mode.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Step through each synchronization point to confirm a post's Wait-code placement aligns channels correctly; mismatched/missing sync points indicate a post defect.

surfaces.label: Previous
surfaces.action: Jumps to the previous synchronization point (Wait code) in Multi Channel mode.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Reverse traversal of sync points for the same Wait-code verification as Next.

surfaces.label: Setup Multi Channel
surfaces.path: NC-Assistant > Multi Channel > Setup Multi Channel
surfaces.action: Opens the Multi Channel configuration dialog in the Editor Setup (also reachable via the setup icon). Multi Channel must be configured per file type before use.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Configures channel/wait-code definitions per file type — prerequisite so the Multi Channel sync verification reflects the real machine's channel structure.

surfaces.label: Synchronize Scrolling
surfaces.action: Locks scrolling so all channel windows scroll together.

surfaces.label: Window
surfaces.action: Views the current program in Multi Channel mode (channels side-by-side in separate editor windows with Wait-code synchronization). Requires Multi Channel configured in Editor Setup for the file type.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Core proving aid for multi-channel/multi-spindle machines: opens synchronized channel view so an agent can verify a post correctly emits matching Wait codes (yellow=matched, purple=missing) across channels.

surfaces.label: Hide NC-Assistant formula results
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > General > NC-Assistant > Hide NC-Assistant formula results
surfaces.action: Checkbox: hides the result fields of NC-Assistant macro formulas in the Insert dialog. Global setting; overrides the per-macro 'Hide formula results' option in Macro Setup.

surfaces.label: Show NC-Assistant suggestions on keyboard input
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > General > NC-Assistant > Show NC-Assistant suggestions on keyboard input
surfaces.action: Checkbox: enables an autocomplete dropdown of NC-Assistant macro suggestions as you type in the Editor.

surfaces.label: Suppress NC-Assistant
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > General > NC-Assistant > Suppress NC-Assistant
surfaces.action: Checkbox: hides the NC-Assistant sidebar including macros and disables the show/hide options under the NC-Assistant Info tab.

surfaces.label: Macro Setup
surfaces.action: Opens the Macro Setup dialog to configure, add and modify macros for different file types.

surfaces.label: Record Macro
surfaces.action: Creates a macro from a selected NC block: select block, click Record Macro, name it in the Add Macro dialog, OK opens Macro Setup for further config.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Could capture a golden block from a known-good NC file as a macro, then use Find Macro to assert the same block appears (byte/pattern match) in a post-regenerated file.

surfaces.label: NC-Assistant
surfaces.action: Top-level ribbon tab gathering macro insert/modify/find, macro selection, sidebar/balloon toggles, macro setup, and multi-channel view tools.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Entry point for macro-driven NC code editing; macros are how CIMCO recognizes/parameterizes specific NC blocks, relevant for verifying that a post-emitted block matches a known macro pattern.

surfaces.label: Advanced Renumbering
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Block Numbers > Advanced Renumbering
surfaces.action: Rule/trigger/label-driven renumbering for complex NC code; saves reusable rule groups per control type and can output the result to a new window.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Control-type-specific renumbering (incl. G70 finishing-cycle P/Q label preservation) lets the agent reproduce a controller's exact numbering scheme so proven NC matches the machine's expected block structure before drip-feed.

surfaces.label: Configure Block Numbering
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Block Numbers > Configure Block Numbering
surfaces.action: Opens the Block Numbers configuration dialog in Editor Setup for the current file type.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Entry point to set the per-file-type numbering rules a post must emit; configured before proving so renumber output matches the target controller convention.

surfaces.label: Remove
surfaces.action: Deletes all block numbers from the NC program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Stripping all N-numbers normalizes two programs to a number-agnostic form so a byte/structure compare vs golden ignores numbering differences.

surfaces.label: Renumber
surfaces.action: Inserts block numbers into the NC program, or renumbers existing ones; if 'Show quick setup' is enabled a quick-setup dialog appears for swift configuration.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Normalizes block numbering so a generated post output can be byte-compared against a golden file that uses consistent N-numbering; mismatched/absent block numbers otherwise cause false diffs.

surfaces.label: Combined Tool List
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Info > Combined Tool List
surfaces.action: Generates a combined tool list across two or more open NC programs into a new document.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Aggregates tooling across multiple proven programs for setup verification / multi-op job validation.

surfaces.label: Configure Tool List
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Info > Configure Tool List
surfaces.action: Opens the Tool List configuration (Editor Setup > Tool List) to control how tool lists are generated.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Configures tool-list output format so generated lists match the expected golden format before comparison.

surfaces.label: Make Tool List
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Info > Make Tool List
surfaces.action: Generates a tool list from the current NC program into a new document.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Extracts the tool set a post emitted; comparing the generated tool list vs an expected/golden list verifies the post output the correct T-numbers/tool sequence.

surfaces.label: Toolpath Graphs
surfaces.area: NC Functions > Info > Toolpath Statistics dialog
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Info > Toolpath Statistics > Graph
surfaces.action: Plots per-axis position over time (one colored line per axis) plus feedrate, to catch irregularities not obvious in code; axis/feed toggles, absolute/delta values, zoom modes.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Visual axis-vs-time + feed plot surfaces discontinuities/spikes in a post's output (e.g. bad rapids, feed glitches) during prove-out; GUI-only so an agent reads the underlying stats rather than the plot.

surfaces.label: Toolpath Statistics
surfaces.action: Shows per-tool X/Y/Z range, machining time, tool-change time, toolpath length etc.; recomputes live on unit/tool-change-time/rapid-speed changes; exports data and opens Toolpath Graphs.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Computes X/Y/Z travel range and per-tool extents from the NC — the agent reads these to check the program stays within machine limits, and compares cycle-time/length stats of post output vs golden as a regression signal. CSV export gives a machine-readable proving artifact.

surfaces.label: Auto Insert Spaces
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Auto Insert Spaces
surfaces.action: Toggle: when active, a space is automatically inserted before each NC-word for programs written without spaces.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Ensures NC-words are tokenizable/spaced so downstream parsing or compare of post output behaves deterministically.

surfaces.label: Insert Block Skips
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Block Skips
surfaces.action: Prepends the block-skip character to selected lines, or to all lines if none selected. Skip character defined in Machine configuration.
fields: (applies to selection or whole program; char from Machine config)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Block-skip (/) handling must round-trip correctly through a post; inserting/verifying skip chars helps prove the post preserves optional-skip blocks.

surfaces.label: Insert Monitoring Macros
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Strings (down arrow) > Insert Monitoring Macros
surfaces.action: Auto-detects program start, feedrate (F), spindle speed (S), tool change (T) and inserts DPRNT lines after each; values readable via serial interface.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: DPRNT monitoring macros emit F/S/T/start values over serial during a real run, enabling live verification of what the machine actually executed vs the proven NC.

surfaces.label: Insert Spaces
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Spaces
surfaces.action: Inserts a space between adjacent NC commands where none exists; existing spaces untouched.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Whitespace normalization: aligns spacing so a proven post's output can be diffed against a golden that uses spaced words.

surfaces.label: Insert Strings
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Strings
surfaces.action: Inserts a user-defined string at a chosen position relative to lines/block numbers/matched text; supports plain or regex line matching.
fields: Where: Insert at start of line
Where: Insert at end of line
Where: Insert after block number / Replace matched string
Where: Insert on new line before matched string
Where: Insert on new line after matched string
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Programmatic injection of required machine-specific lines (e.g. safe-start blocks, M-codes) to bring a post's output up to a proven golden, or to patch test fixtures.

surfaces.label: Lowercase
surfaces.action: Converts all text (including comments) to lowercase.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Case normalization for tolerant compare of generated vs golden NC.

surfaces.label: Mark/Delete Range
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Mark/Delete Range
surfaces.action: Opens a dialog to specify a range of lines or block numbers to select/update/delete; can select/delete from a tool-change, feedrate or spindle-speed value up to the next. Also reachable from Editor > Edit menu.
fields: Special selection from tool change / feedrate / spindle speed value to next
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets the agent isolate one tool's segment of an NC program (tool-change to tool-change) for targeted sim or comparison of a single operation against golden.

surfaces.label: Remove Block Skips
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Block Skips (down arrow) > Remove Block Skips
surfaces.action: Removes all block-skip characters from the NC program (or only selected lines if a selection exists).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Normalizes away optional-skip markers so a byte-compare vs golden isn't tripped by skip-char differences.

surfaces.label: Remove Comments
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Spaces (down arrow) > Remove Comments
surfaces.action: Removes all comments (parentheses or the Comment start/end chars defined in Machine configuration) from the NC program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Strips comments (date stamps, post version banners) that legitimately differ between runs, so a proving compare focuses only on motion/command code.

surfaces.label: Remove Empty Lines
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Spaces (down arrow) > Remove Empty Lines
surfaces.action: Removes all empty lines from the NC program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Blank-line normalization before structural compare of generated vs golden NC.

surfaces.label: Remove Monitoring Macros
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Strings (down arrow) > Remove Monitoring Macros
surfaces.action: Removes all DPRNT lines added by Insert Monitoring Macros, restoring the original NC program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Reverts instrumented NC back to the clean program after a monitored prove-out run before final byte-compare.

surfaces.label: Remove Spaces
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Spaces (down arrow) > Remove Spaces
surfaces.action: Deletes all space and tab (whitespace) characters from the NC program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Collapses whitespace to a canonical form for tolerant byte-compare between post output and golden NC.

surfaces.label: Remove Strings
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Insert / Remove > Insert Strings (down arrow) > Remove Strings
surfaces.action: Removes strings from the NC program per the Remove String dialog (mirrors Insert Strings dialog, incl. regex matching).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Strips run-variant tokens (timestamps, IDs) before byte-compare so only meaningful post differences remain.

surfaces.label: Uppercase
surfaces.action: Converts all text (including comments) to UPPERCASE.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Case normalization so a case-insensitive controller's NC compares cleanly against golden regardless of post output case.

surfaces.label: Block Numbers (Editor Setup)
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Block Numbers
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Block Numbers
surfaces.action: Per-file-type configuration of NC line numbering: renumber behavior and block number format. Settings apply only to the File Type shown at top of dialog.
fields: Disable undo prompt for large files
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the exact N-numbering scheme (char, format, interval, restart triggers, skip rules) a controller expects; the agent sets these per file type so renumbered post output matches golden block numbering before byte-compare/drip-feed. Stored in the file-type/editor config so it is file-channel addressable.

surfaces.label: NC Functions
surfaces.action: Ribbon tab grouping Block Numbers, Insert/Remove, Transform and Info command groups for editing/analyzing the open NC program.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Top-level container for the NC-editing surfaces a post-proving agent drives to manipulate/inspect generated G-code before sim/byte-compare.

surfaces.label: Adjust Feedrate
surfaces.action: Scales feedrate values in the NC program by a percentage (slider or field), with clamping and conditional ranges.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets the agent derive a known-scaled NC variant to verify a post correctly emits/clamps feedrates, or to compare optimized vs baseline feed output.

surfaces.label: Adjust spindle speed
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Transform > Adjust spindle speed
surfaces.action: Scales spindle-speed values in the NC program by a percentage (slider or field), with clamping and conditional ranges.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Verifies a post emits/clamps S-values correctly; produces controlled S variants for comparison against golden.

surfaces.label: Convert NC code
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Transform > Convert NC code
surfaces.action: Converts one NC format to another using a .conv converter/post-processor file (CIMCO ships some in \Converters); can target NCI and longhand cycles.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Core post-proving lever: re-post an NC/NCI through a target converter (.conv) and compare against golden; 'Use longhand cycles' expands canned cycles for a movement-level comparison; NCI is the intermediate proving format.

surfaces.label: Heidenhain / ISO Converter
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Transform > Heidenhain / ISO Converter
surfaces.action: Converts Heidenhain conversational programs to ISO G-code and vice versa.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Cross-dialect conversion lets the agent transform a Heidenhain golden into ISO (or back) to byte/structure-compare against an ISO post's output for the same part.

surfaces.label: Mirror
surfaces.action: Mirrors the program outline about a defined axis (with a turning-program mode that disables the user axis), plus arc-type/number-format options and toolpath reversal.
fields: Arc type (Auto detect / Relative to start / Relative to end / Absolute arc center)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Mirrored toolpaths (incl. turning-mode) test that a post emits correct G41/G42 sides and arc senses; produces variants for sim/compare.

surfaces.label: Rotate
surfaces.action: Rotates the program outline about a point by a given angle, with arc-type and number-format options and optional toolpath reversal.
fields: Arc type (Auto detect / Relative to start / Relative to end / Absolute arc center)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Generates rotated toolpath variants for sim/compare and for verifying the post handles arc directions and modal state under rotation.

surfaces.label: Show Windows Calculator
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Transform > Show Windows Calculator
surfaces.action: Opens the Windows calculator.

surfaces.label: Simple math functions
surfaces.path: NC Functions > Transform > Simple math functions
surfaces.action: Applies +/-/x/division to selected NC parameters with min/max clamping, decimal control and case scoping.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Mathematically transform axis/parameter words to construct deterministic test fixtures or rescale coordinates, useful for verifying a post's numeric formatting (decimals, leading/trailing zero handling) against golden.

surfaces.label: Tool compensation
surfaces.action: Applies cutter compensation offset left (G41) or right (G42) to the programmed contour based on feed direction, with arc-type and number-format options.
fields: Arc type (Auto detect / Relative to start / Relative to end / Absolute arc center)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Verifies a post correctly emits G41/G42 cutter-comp and offset geometry; lets the agent generate comp'd contours to compare against a golden machine-comp output.

surfaces.label: Translate
surfaces.action: Offsets the program outline by X/Y/Z values, with arc-type interpretation and number-format options.
fields: Arc type (Auto detect / Relative to start / Relative to end / Absolute arc center)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Shifting coordinates (with correct arc-center handling) lets the agent reposition a proven toolpath to a new datum and re-verify post/sim output, or test G90/G91 + arc-mode correctness.

surfaces.label: Presentation Viewer (stand-alone)
surfaces.action: Stand-alone simulation viewer app; opens saved simulation files / presentation bundles without CIMCO Edit installed. Window = Ribbon (top), 3D viewport (center), info panels (left), axis control (right), playback/timeline (bottom). All panels mirror CIMCO Edit.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: A headless/standalone way to replay an archived proof: a saved simulation file can be opened in the viewer (launchable as a separate exe) to inspect collisions/positions of a proven post without the full editor.

surfaces.label: Axis Control Panel
surfaces.action: Manual axis positioning via sliders + numeric readouts for X/Y/Z and optional A/B/C; allows manual inspection, collision checking, reach demonstration, positioning independent of program execution.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets a proof manually drive axes to test machine reach / travel limits independent of the posted program (limit validation).

surfaces.label: NC Program Panel
surfaces.path: Presentation Viewer > Information Panels > NC Program
surfaces.action: Displays NC program lines, highlights the currently executed block, auto-scrolls during playback.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Synchronizes posted NC lines with simulated motion so an agent can map any collision/position event back to the exact posted block.

surfaces.label: Tool Position and Status Panel
surfaces.path: Presentation Viewer > Information Panels > Tool Position and Status
surfaces.action: Shows current tool position X/Y/Z + optional rotary A/B/C (mm and degrees) updating live, plus active tool number, feedrate, spindle speed, elapsed time, and total machining time.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Live readout for proving a post: confirm posted coordinates, feed (F), spindle (S), and total cycle time match expectation at each block — cycle-time validation and per-block position verification via UIA.

surfaces.label: Playback & Timeline Controls
surfaces.action: Simulation execution controls: play, pause, step forward/backward, fast forward, rewind, start/end navigation, adjustable playback speed, timeline scrubber. Identical behavior in CIMCO Edit Simulation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The driver for a blind proof run: step/play through the posted program block-by-block (with stop-on-collision) and scrub to any event timestamp — same controls in CIMCO Edit Simulation, so the proof loop is identical in both apps.

surfaces.label: Collision Checking
surfaces.action: Collision checking panel: real-time detection of collisions between tool, holder, workpiece, stock, and machine components, with configurable checking options and a detailed, time-stamped collision event list.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: THE collision oracle in the viewer: a time-stamped collision event list is the machine-readable crash record for a posted program; empty list = collision-clean proof. GUI-only — read via UIA.

surfaces.label: Compare (Stock Compare)
surfaces.action: Enables stock comparison view: current stock state vs a reference stock using color mapping and tolerance settings. Equivalent to Stock Compare in CIMCO Edit.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Core post-proof oracle for geometry correctness: color-mapped deviation of the cut stock vs the reference/design proves the posted program removes the right material within tolerance (catches overcut/undercut a collision check misses).

surfaces.label: Cross Section
surfaces.action: Movable section plane dynamically cutting stock/tool/workpiece for inspection; adjustable plane position and orientation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Inspect interior geometry (pockets/bores) of the proof result to verify the posted program reached internal features correctly.

surfaces.label: Fixture
surfaces.action: Displays fixtures: vises, clamps, tombstones, custom fixturing.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Fixtures are collision targets — including them proves the posted program avoids clamps/tombstones.

surfaces.label: Machine Simulation (viewer)
surfaces.action: Enables full machine kinematics in the viewer.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Activates machine-component collision/limit checking for the posted program inside the stand-alone proof replay.

surfaces.label: Measure Distance
surfaces.action: Measures distances directly in the 3D scene.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Verify a dimension on the proof result matches the print (manual measurement of cut geometry).

surfaces.label: Quality
surfaces.action: Side panel controlling surface-quality visualization; adjustable low-to-high quality level and True Vision toggle for realistic surface appearance.

surfaces.label: Show / Hide Base
surfaces.path: Presentation Viewer > Ribbon > Show / Hide Base
surfaces.action: Toggles visibility of the machine base/frame.

surfaces.label: Show / Hide Controls
surfaces.path: Presentation Viewer > Ribbon > Show / Hide Controls
surfaces.action: Toggles UI overlays in the viewport.

surfaces.label: Show / Hide Head
surfaces.path: Presentation Viewer > Ribbon > Show / Hide Head
surfaces.action: Toggles visibility of the spindle / head.

surfaces.label: Show / Hide Table
surfaces.path: Presentation Viewer > Ribbon > Show / Hide Table
surfaces.action: Toggles visibility of the machine table.

surfaces.label: Stock
surfaces.action: Controls visibility and visualization of the stock model.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Toggles the stock model whose final state is compared against the design — central to stock-compare proof.

surfaces.label: Stop Conditions
surfaces.action: Defines simulation stop rules: tool change, block, collision.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Stop-on-collision turns the proof into a deterministic halt at the first crash; stop-on-tool-change / stop-on-block let an agent step a posted program operation-by-operation.

surfaces.label: Tool
surfaces.action: Displays the active tool assembly (cutter + holder).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Confirms the tool assembly active at any block of the posted program during proof inspection.

surfaces.label: Toolpath
surfaces.action: Toolpath visualization menu: show/hide toolpath plus multiple visualization and animation modes.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Renders the motion path of the posted NC for visual verification of rapids, feeds, retracts and link moves.

surfaces.label: View
surfaces.action: Standard camera views (Top, Front, Isometric, etc.).

surfaces.label: Workpiece
surfaces.action: Defines and displays the raw stock geometry.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Sets/inspects the workpiece used for the proof; the reference for material-removal validation.

surfaces.label: Zoom Window
surfaces.action: Box-zoom into a selected area of the viewport.

surfaces.label: Save Presentation
surfaces.action: Exports the complete simulation either as a simulation file (data only) or as a presentation bundle (data + viewer app) for sharing/archiving. Compact, suited to archiving alongside setup sheets and tool lists.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Captures a proof run to a portable file — the artifact a CI/blind pipeline produces as evidence that the posted NC simulated cleanly, archivable next to the NC and golden files.

surfaces.label: Advanced Machine Configuration Editor
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Custom Machines > Advanced Machine Editor
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > Custom Machines > Advanced Machine Editor
surfaces.action: Simplified machine-model editor that auto-builds setup and auto-calculates kinematics from chosen axis arrangement, with real-time preview. Cannot do collinear axes/revolvers/spindles (use the full editor for those).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Faster way to define a machine model (axes, travel limits, feedrates, STL models, tool-change positions, tool-change NC) for limit/collision proving; produces the same MachineCfg files (channel:file).
fields: Properties section: machine Name, Type, Unit System, Head/Table axis config
Models section: STL list (+ add), axes assignment, color, visibility
Axes section: Travel limit (min/max), Feedrate, Position; animate preview play button
Tool Change Positions: per-axis order (1st/2nd/...) + target position
NC-Commands: inject NC code on tool change

surfaces.label: Backplot configuration (Editor Setup)
surfaces.action: Per-File-Type backplot/simulation configuration dialog: select CNC control + machine config, tool library, sim version, enhanced quality, turning config, export. Applies only to the currently selected File Type.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The prerequisite setup before any post can be proven: defines which control dialect interprets the NC and which machine model collisions/limits are checked against. Misconfigured Control Type = invalid proof.

surfaces.label: Automatically import tools from a tool library
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Automatically import tools from a tool library
surfaces.action: Checkbox to auto-load tools from a specified library when simulation starts.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Ensures the posted NC's tools have real assembly geometry at proof time without manual loading — needed for accurate tool/holder collision proof.

surfaces.label: Control Type
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Control Type
surfaces.action: Dropdown selecting the CNC control for the file type (e.g. 'ISO Milling'); defines controller-specific syntax/commands used to interpret and simulate the NC. Configurable further under Control Settings.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Single most important post-proof setting: the control dialect must match the post's target controller (Fanuc/Haas/Siemens/etc.) or the simulation mis-parses the posted G-code and the proof is meaningless.

surfaces.label: Enable enhanced quality (Beta)
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Enable enhanced quality (Beta)
surfaces.action: Checkbox enabling the new enhancing algorithm in simulation. Enabled by default; Fast-version only. Disables 'Refine edges' option.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Improves surface/stock fidelity of the proof; affects which stock-verification options are valid (Refine edges unavailable when on).

surfaces.label: Export (.MacBundle)
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Export > Export
surfaces.action: Exports the control + machine configuration for the selected File Type as a .MacBundle (Machine Bundle) file, importable on another PC. Prompts for File Type at export.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets a known-good control+machine proof setup be captured to a .MacBundle and replicated headlessly across machines/CI so the post-proof environment is reproducible.

surfaces.label: Highlight syntax errors when backplotting
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Highlight syntax errors when backplotting
surfaces.action: Checkbox to highlight code errors in the program during Backplot/Machine Simulation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Surfaces post-emitted syntax errors inline during proof; pairs with the Simulation Report to mark which posted lines are malformed.

surfaces.label: Machine Configuration Editor
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Machine Setup > [machine icon]
surfaces.action: Editor for custom machine configurations (kinematics/components), opened from the machine icon. Only custom machines editable.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Where the machine kinematic model used for collision/limit proof is built or edited; correct component tree is what makes machine-component collision detection valid.

surfaces.label: Machine Setup (4/5-Axis)
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Machine Setup
surfaces.action: Dropdown selecting a machine configuration for the file type. Machine icon next to dropdown opens the Machine Configuration Editor (custom machines only are editable).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Loads the kinematic machine model that Machine Simulation checks collisions and axis limits against — required to prove a 4/5-axis post moves a real machine without crash or over-travel.

surfaces.label: Simulation Window (version)
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Simulation Window
surfaces.action: Dropdown selecting the simulation engine: Standard or Fast (default).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Selects the engine that runs the post-proof; Fast is default and required for enhanced-quality verification.

surfaces.label: Tool Library
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Tool Library
surfaces.action: Dropdown selecting the tool library from which tools are auto-loaded (assemblies/cutters/holders visible in Tool Manager). Maps to a .tmlib tool-library file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The tool-geometry source for proof; a .tmlib can be written/selected directly (file channel) so a blind agent supplies the correct cutters+holders the posted program calls (T-numbers).

surfaces.label: Turning Configuration
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Turning > Turning Configuration
surfaces.action: List of orientation configurations for turning; default selected unless a trigger added to another config matches a supplied text file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Sets lathe orientation for proving a turning post so axis directions/views match the posted program's intended setup.

surfaces.label: Orientation (Turning)
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Turning > Orientation
surfaces.action: Field specifying the orientation of the selected turning configuration.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Aligns the simulated lathe coordinate orientation to the posted program so turning toolpaths render correctly during proof.

surfaces.label: Trigger (Turning)
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Turning > Trigger
surfaces.action: Field setting the trigger text for the selected turning orientation configuration (auto-selects config when matching text found in file).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Enables auto-selection of the right turning orientation when proving posted NC whose header contains the trigger string.

surfaces.label: Colors
surfaces.action: Per-File-Type syntax-highlighting / color setup: define and prioritize color rules incl. rapid/linear/arc move colors and file-compare colors.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: 'File compare background for different lines/text' + 'File compare color for missing lines' colors drive the visual diff used when comparing proved NC vs golden NC; modal move colors (rapid/linear/G2/G3) aid visual inspection of backplot-vs-program correspondence.
fields: List of colors (listbox: Text/Background/Block/Comments/Text-in-blocks/Rapid/Linear/CW arc G2/CCW arc G3/file-compare colors/Imported-file bg/Highlighted-line bg/Syntax-error text+bg/Multi-channel colors/diff wave)
Apply color to the entire line (checkbox)

surfaces.label: Control Settings
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Backplot > Control Settings
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > File Types > Backplot > Control Settings
surfaces.action: Configure control-specific parameters for the control selected for the current File Type; stored with the File Type (does not overwrite the control config itself).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The control parameters determine how the simulator interprets the NC dialect during proving — getting these right per File Type is part of validating that the post output simulates correctly for that machine/control.
fields: Control Settings (listbox of per-control parameters; per-parameter description shown at dialog bottom)

surfaces.label: Custom Machines
surfaces.action: Create, configure, edit, and delete custom machine configurations (the kinematic model used by Machine Simulation).
fields: List of Machines (all available custom machines)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Where a non-stock/JM-specific machine gets defined so a post can be proven against the real shop machine kinematics rather than a generic system model.

surfaces.label: Add (New Machine)
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Custom Machines > Add dialog
surfaces.action: Opens the Add dialog to create a new machine: name + axis/rotational type, then opens the Advanced Machine Configuration Editor.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines axis count/rotary configuration that the post must match; proving a 5-axis post requires the matching 5-axis Head/Table kinematic config selected here.

surfaces.label: Advanced Edit (Advanced Machine Configuration Editor)
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > Custom Machines > Advanced Edit
surfaces.action: Opens the Advanced Machine Configuration Editor for the selected machine; can auto-build most of the setup for the user.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Editor where machine kinematics/limits are authored — the limits/collision geometry the simulation uses to flag a bad post. Underlying config is a machine-config file editable via the file channel.

surfaces.label: Delete
surfaces.action: Deletes the selected custom machine.

surfaces.label: Edit (Machine Configuration Editor)
surfaces.action: Opens the (basic) Machine Configuration Editor for the selected machine; can also create new machines directly.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Direct authoring of the machine config consumed by simulation; the config file itself is the file-channel surface PRISM could write to attach geometry/limits.

surfaces.label: Editor Settings
surfaces.action: Look and behavior of the text editor: scroll bars, line numbers, replace/search behavior, whitespace, uppercase, block mode, font.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: 'Always UPPER CASE' and 'Replace tabs with space' silently mutate NC text on open/edit — relevant when byte-comparing NC against a golden file (must be off to preserve exact bytes).
fields: Disable Backspace at start of line (checkbox)

surfaces.label: Editor Setup (dialog)
surfaces.action: Two-pane config dialog: left nav menu (with search bar + context-help ? icon), right pane shows the selected section's settings.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The container that hosts machine-model, control, scanning, and backplot config needed to prove a post.
fields: Navigation menu (General, File Types, Global Colors, External Commands, Mazatrol Viewer, Machine Models, Custom Machines, Plugins)

surfaces.label: Setup
surfaces.action: Opens the Editor Setup dialog (root of all configuration).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Entry point to every config screen used to set up a post-proving environment (machine model, control, scanning, backplot).

surfaces.label: Cancel
surfaces.action: Closes Editor Setup without applying changes.

surfaces.label: Default
surfaces.action: Resets CIMCO Edit to its default settings.

surfaces.label: Export
surfaces.action: Exports the entire CIMCO Edit configuration to a .zip file (backup / replicate to other PCs).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets PRISM snapshot/replicate a known-good post-proving config (file-type, machine, control, scanning) as a .zip and re-import it on a clean machine for reproducible proving.

surfaces.label: Help
surfaces.action: Opens the Help dialog.

surfaces.label: Import
surfaces.action: Imports a previously exported configuration .zip (requires restart to apply).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Restores a canonical config so the proving environment is byte-for-byte identical run to run.

surfaces.label: OK
surfaces.action: Closes Editor Setup and applies changes.

surfaces.label: External Commands
surfaces.action: Configure up to 2 command-line calls runnable from NC Functions > Commands menu; supports variables $FILE, $FILENOEXT, $PATH, $FILEPATH, $OUTFILE.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Direct hook to invoke an external post-processor/verifier exe on the current NC file ($FILEPATH) and capture output to $OUTFILE — PRISM can wire its own post-prove/byte-compare tool here and trigger it from the menu, or replicate the same exe+args via CLI.
fields: Command 1/2 Title (text → appears in Commands menu)

surfaces.label: File Types
surfaces.action: Manage File Types (config profiles): list, reorder/sort, delete, rename, copy, add new from a template. The active File Type scopes all sub-sections (Colors, Load/Save, Machine, Backplot, Scanning, etc.).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The File Type selects the default control + machine used for simulation and the scanning rules — choosing the correct File Type is the prerequisite to proving a post for a given machine.

surfaces.label: Add File Type
surfaces.action: Creates a new File Type from a predefined template (enter name, pick template, OK).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Creates a machine/control profile to prove a specific post against.

surfaces.label: General
surfaces.action: General program settings: window behavior, file-handling, language, file-size display, simulation window size, backup, file association.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: 'Default simulation window size' (10-90%, default 66%) and 'Show file size in' (bytes/meter/feet) affect how proving output is displayed; 'Save backup file'/'Backup Extension' control golden-vs-current file retention.
fields: Open files with wrapped lines read only (checkbox)
Default simulation window size (number, % of screen, 10-90, default 66)
Exit editor and save files when inactive (checkbox)

surfaces.label: Associate file extensions
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > General > Associate file extensions
surfaces.action: Re-associates all extensions defined per File Type (.NC, .H, etc.) with CIMCO Edit in Windows.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Ensures NC files under test open in CIMCO Edit (vs another app) when launched by path.

surfaces.label: Global Colors
surfaces.action: Global (not per-File-Type) colors for the simulation/backplot versions and the CNC-Calc add-on.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Sets simulation/backplot rendering colors — affects readability of collision/limit highlighting during proving (visual only, no automation hook).

surfaces.label: Load / Save
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > File Types > Load / Save
surfaces.action: Per-File-Type extension association, default load/save directories, auto-save interval, linefeed type, and UNICODE handling.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: 'Save with linefeed type' (Auto/DOS-CRLF/Unix-LF/Mac-CR) and the UNICODE save options directly determine the byte content of saved NC — must match the golden file's encoding/EOL for a clean byte-compare. Default load/save paths let PRISM point proving I/O at known dirs.
fields: Save with linefeed type (dropdown: Auto/DOS-Windows CRLF/Unix LF/Mac CR)
Prompt to save files as UNICODE (checkbox)
Always save files as regular text (checkbox)

surfaces.label: Machine (File-Type machine settings)
surfaces.action: Per-File-Type config of program characters, NC code prefixes, and units used throughout the editor and backplot/simulation. Applies only to the currently selected File Type.
fields: Use decimal point on numeric keypad
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: These settings tell the backplot/simulation how to PARSE the NC (comment delimiters, tool-change/feed/speed prefixes) and which UNITS to use — wrong unit here is a 25.4x scale error in the sim. Must match the post's dialect before the sim result is trustworthy. The File-Type config is stored in a CIMCO config file, so PRISM can set these via the file channel rather than the GUI.

surfaces.label: Machine Configuration Editor
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Custom Machines > Machine Configuration Editor
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > Custom Machines > Machine Configuration Editor
surfaces.action: Full machine-model editor: build a hierarchical component tree (Base/Head/Table/axes/tool-changer/geometry) with limits, feedrates, tool-change sequence; supports collinear axes, turrets/revolvers, spindles. Saves configs to MachineCfg dir.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the machine kinematics, axis travel LIMITS and feedrates the simulation checks against — essential for proving a post does not violate axis limits or collide. Configs are files in \AppData\Roaming\...\MachineCfg\ that PRISM could author/inspect directly (channel:file).
fields: Save (button; red icon = errors, green = ok)
Add Geometry / Add Linear Axis / Add Rotational Axis / Delete buttons
Right-click: Add Collinear Axis / Add Spindle / Add Turret
Base props: Name, Unit System, Orientation, Maximum Cutting Feedrate (mm/min), Acceleration (Slow/Medium/Fast), Work Origin, Home Position (G53/M91)
Rotary Axis props: Address(A/B/C), Limits(deg), Feedrate(deg/min), Direction, Centre of Rotation(XYZ)
Linear Axis props: Address(X/Y/Z), Limits, Feedrate(mm/min), Direction
Collinear Axis props: Address(U/V/W), Limits, Feedrate, Direction
Geometry props: File Path(STL), Unit System, Color(RGB 0-255)
Tool Changer (Chain) props: Sequence, Position, NC-Commands
Tool Changer (Turret) props: Mount Axis, Direction, Center, Number of Slots, Slot 1-64 (XYZ)
Preview button (Machine Preview 3D + Axis Control panel)

surfaces.label: Machine Preview
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > Custom Machines > Machine Configuration Editor > Preview
surfaces.action: 3D preview of the machine; rotate (LMB), zoom (wheel), pan (RMB); toggle Head/Table/Base visibility; test axis travel limits via Axis Control panel.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets you visually verify axis travel ranges before relying on them for limit-checking during proving (GUI-only, no automation hook).

surfaces.label: Machine Models
surfaces.action: Download/install/uninstall machine models for the Machine Simulation add-on; only visible when Machine Simulation is activated.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Gates whether ANY machine model exists to simulate against — to prove a post you must first Install the relevant system machine model here. The installed model is the simulation target for collision/limit checks. GUI-only manager (no documented .mcfg path on this page); installed models land on disk and would then be loadable as files.

surfaces.label: Check for updates at launch
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > Machine Models > Check for updates at launch
surfaces.action: Toggles a startup notification when an installed machine model has a newer version.

surfaces.label: Install
surfaces.action: Installs all machines whose Install-column checkbox is enabled.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Required pre-step to have a system machine model present for simulation; without an installed model there is nothing to load for the post-proving sim.

surfaces.label: Uninstall
surfaces.action: Uninstalls all selected (checkbox-enabled) machines.

surfaces.label: Update
surfaces.action: Queries/reloads the list of downloadable machines from the CIMCO server.

surfaces.label: View Notes
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > Machine Models > View Notes
surfaces.action: Shows the full modification/release-note history of the selected machine model.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets an agent confirm the exact model version/release before trusting its kinematics for a post-proving sim.

surfaces.label: Set feedrate prefix
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > NC Codes
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > NC Codes > Set feedrate
surfaces.action: Specifies the feedrate prefix (e.g. F) used to parse feed values from the NC.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets the sim read feeds the post emits; needed if proving feed correctness / cycle-time against the machine model.

surfaces.label: Rapid speed (mm/min)
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > Units
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > Units > Rapid speed
surfaces.action: Sets the default rapid feedrate used by backplot/simulation cycle-time estimation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Affects simulated cycle-time; relevant only if proving a post against time estimates, not geometry/collisions.

surfaces.label: Set spindle speed prefix
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > NC Codes
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > NC Codes > Set spindle speed
surfaces.action: Specifies the spindle-speed prefix (e.g. S) used to parse RPM from the NC.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets the sim read spindle speeds the post emits; relevant when proving speed/limit handling.

surfaces.label: Tool Change prefix
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > NC Codes
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > NC Codes > Tool Change
surfaces.action: Specifies the tool-change prefix (e.g. T for T010101) the parser uses to detect tool changes.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: If the sim cannot identify tool changes it cannot apply the right tool geometry — proving a post means the sim must recognize every tool change emitted by the post.

surfaces.label: Toolpath unit
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > Units
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Machine > Units > Toolpath unit
surfaces.action: Selects inch vs mm measurement unit used throughout CIMCO Edit including the backplot/simulation.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: UNITS-FIRST gate: a mismatch between this and the NC (G20/G21) yields a 25.4x scale error in the simulation, invalidating any collision/limit/byte-compare result. Must be resolved from the NC source before proving the post.

surfaces.label: Mazatrol Viewer setup
surfaces.action: Configures how Mazatrol binary files are displayed and associates file extensions with Mazak CNC controls. Viewer is view/print only (no edit/save back to binary); it is a separately-licensed add-on enabled under Plugins.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: For Mazak/Mazatrol-conversational targets, the viewer is the only way to read the binary program; since it cannot write back, post proving of Mazatrol is view/print-verify only (channel uia) — note this limitation.

surfaces.label: Mazatrol file-extension Associations
surfaces.action: List associating specific file extensions with Mazak CNC controls; managed via Add, Edit, Delete buttons.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Associating the right extension with the right Mazak control ensures the viewer decodes a Mazatrol post-output binary correctly before view/print proving.

surfaces.label: Mazatrol Viewer Decimals
surfaces.path: Setup > Mazatrol Viewer > Mazatrol Viewer Decimals
surfaces.action: Number of decimal places used to display values in the Mazatrol Viewer.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Decimal display precision affects whether displayed Mazatrol coordinate values match a golden reference when visually proving a Mazatrol program.

surfaces.label: Mazatrol Viewer Font settings
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Mazatrol Viewer > Font settings
surfaces.action: Preview field shows the selected font; font button opens a font picker for the Mazatrol display.

surfaces.label: Mazatrol Viewer Language
surfaces.action: Dropdown selecting the language used when displaying Mazatrol data.

surfaces.label: Show TPC Data
surfaces.path: Setup > Mazatrol Viewer > Show TPC Data
surfaces.action: Toggles inclusion of TPC data when viewing Mazatrol files.

surfaces.label: Multi Channel
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel
surfaces.action: Per-File-Type config of how CIMCO identifies multi-channel program codes and lays channels out side-by-side with wait-code synchronization.
fields: Multi channel mode (dropdown: predefined types or User Defined)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: For multi-channel (twin-spindle/turret or multi-channel mill-turn) posts, the sim/view must split channels correctly before proving; wrong Channel start/end means the post output is mis-parsed and the proof is invalid.

surfaces.label: Multi Channel Configuration
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel > Multi Channel Configuration
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel > Configure
surfaces.action: Configures the synchronization commands (sync points/wait codes) used to align channels in a multi-channel NC program.
fields: List of Synchronization Commands (expression / Channel Number / Channel Number Trigger)
Synchronization Command (String or Advanced/RegEx, e.g. M3<[0-9][0-9]>)
Extract channel from line (checkbox enables trigger)
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Sync/wait codes are exactly what proves a multi-channel post is correctly choreographed — matching wait codes render yellow, missing ones purple, surfacing post synchronization errors visually (a UIA-readable proof signal).

surfaces.label: Load template
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel > Load template
surfaces.action: Loads a previously saved multi-channel template.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Reapplies a known-good channel-parsing config before proving a multi-channel post.

surfaces.label: Multi channel mode
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel > Multi channel mode
surfaces.action: Selects a predefined multi-channel command set or User Defined to hand-define channel start/end/sync.
fields: dropdown: predefined controller types | User Defined
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Picking the matching predefined controller is the fastest path to correctly parsing a multi-channel post for proving.

surfaces.label: Save as template
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel > Save as template
surfaces.action: Saves the current multi-channel configuration as a reusable named template.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets a proven multi-channel parsing config be persisted (as a template file) and reloaded per machine — reproducible setup for repeated post proofs.

surfaces.label: Template editor
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel
surfaces.path: Editor Setup > File Types > Multi Channel > Template editor
surfaces.action: Opens the Template Editor (same options as Multi Channel Configuration) to edit saved multi-channel templates.
fields: same fields as Multi Channel Configuration

surfaces.label: Navigation
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Scanning > Navigation
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > File Types > Scanning > Navigation
surfaces.action: Defines the keyword tree (max depth 8, one child per branch) scanned from NC-program comments to build the Backplot Navigation tab tree; load/save the navigation template file.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Builds a tool-change/operation tree by scanning NC comments — lets an agent navigate the proved program structure (jump to each tool change/operation) without screenshots. Requires 'Scan for navigation information' enabled in Scanning. Template is a loadable/savable file.

surfaces.label: Other
surfaces.action: Per-File-Type misc: print columns, max-line-length indicator, insert-spaces-on-open, and Export-Toolpath-as-DXF settings.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: 'Export turning toolpath in XY-plane' + 'Always linearize arcs' + 'Arc quality tolerance' govern the DXF dump of a backplotted toolpath — a DXF export of the proved path can be compared against a golden geometry. 'Insert spaces when opening file' mutates NC text (off for byte-exact compare).

surfaces.label: Plugins
surfaces.action: Enable/disable modules & add-ons (Backplot, advanced/solid simulation, DNC/Serial, File compare, advanced NC-Functions, NC-Base, DNC-Max Client, CNC-Calc, Mazatrol Viewer); set config password and config file paths.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Backplot, advanced (solid) simulation, and DNC/Serial must be ENABLED (not disabled) for proving via simulation and drip-feed; disabling Backplot removes the Backplot tab. 'Edit configuration paths' relocates config dirs PRISM may need to read/write.
fields: Set password (button; Ctrl+Shift on startup to bypass forgotten pw)
Edit configuration paths (button → path dropdown + path field + copy/revert option)

surfaces.label: Edit configuration paths
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > Plugins > Edit configuration paths
surfaces.action: Change the directories CIMCO Edit uses for configuration files (pick a path from dropdown, set new path, optionally copy existing files or revert to default).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets PRISM redirect CIMCO's config to a controlled directory it can read/write for reproducible proving setups.

surfaces.label: Printing
surfaces.action: Print layout: paper size, fonts, headers/footers (with %p/%P/%f/%F/%t/%d/%c/%U tokens), multi-column, raw-print/form-feed options.
fields: Send form feed after last page (checkbox)
Left margin / Right margin (text, cm or 'in')

surfaces.label: Scanning
surfaces.action: Configure how CIMCO loads/saves Scanning Commands (workpiece, fixture, work-offset, tools, holders, geometry) from the NC program or an external .setup sheet, read on simulation start.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: CORE post-proving channel: Scanning Commands are plain text written INTO the NC program or a sibling .setup file (channel:file) that auto-load and place the workpiece/fixture/tool/holder/WCS into the simulation. PRISM can author a .setup sidecar (or inject commands at a trigger keyword) to fully arrange a sim for collision/limit proving with no GUI clicks.
fields: Scan for tool/holder/geometry information (dropdown: Disabled / Auto-prefer-NC / Auto-prefer-setup / Always NC file / Always setup sheet)
Read: Scan for navigation information (checkbox; enables Navigation)
Write: tool/holder/stock/work-offset/geometry info on Save Setup (5 checkboxes)
Placement of tool definitions (dropdown: Top of file / At tool change / Custom)
Location of Setup Sheet (dropdown: Same folder / Data folder / Custom)

surfaces.label: Scanning Commands (NC/.setup text format)
surfaces.action: Documented text grammar for TOOL, HOLDER BEGIN/END, WORKPIECE, FIXTURE, WCS commands embedded in NC or .setup files (with X/Y/Z/A/B/C, UM/UI units, RGB color, STL filename, holder segments).
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Gives PRISM the exact authorable text to build a proving setup file blind: place WORKPIECE/FIXTURE STL at coords, define TOOL with holder + dimensions, set WCS work offsets (IDs 0-6) — then simulation auto-loads it for collision/limit/path proving. No GUI needed.
fields: HOLDER BEGIN <id> "<comment>" <UM/UI> FILE="<stl>" / segment rows (upperD,lowerD,length) / HOLDER END
WORKPIECE ID<n> "<stl>" X Y Z A B C <UM/UI> [RGB=r,g,b]
FIXTURE ID<n> "<stl>" X Y Z A B C <UM/UI> [RGB=r,g,b]
WCS ID<0-6> X Y Z A B C

surfaces.label: Tool Scanning
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Scanning > Tool Scanning
surfaces.path: Editor > Setup > File Types > Scanning > Tool Scanning
surfaces.action: Configure the keyword format of the tool Scanning Command for milling and turning (e.g. AO/BL/CPI/AD keywords, tool-line trigger, assembly/holder/cutter keywords). Dialog variant (milling vs turning) depends on the File Type's Control Type.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Defines the exact tool-line grammar PRISM must emit (or parse) in NC/.setup files so tools are recognized and loaded into the sim for proving — keyword naming must match what CIMCO scans for.
fields: Milling: Tool dimension keyword (dropdown + editable keyword)

surfaces.label: Tool List setup (Editor Setup)
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > File Types > Tool List
surfaces.action: Configures, per File Type, how CIMCO scans an NC program to extract and lay out a tool list. Current File Type is shown at the top; settings apply only to that File Type.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Tool-list generation is a direct post-proving artifact: a correct post emits tool-change codes and comments this scanner can parse into a complete tool list — comparing the generated list against a golden list proves the post's tool output.

surfaces.label: Use advanced configuration template for tool lists
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Tool List > Tool List Setup
surfaces.path: Setup > File Types > Tool List > Use advanced configuration template
surfaces.action: Enables the advanced tool-list generator (HTML/XML output) driven by a template file; reveals the Tool list template path and an Edit-template button.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The advanced template defines deterministic, file-driven tool-list output (HTML/XML) — editing the template file directly (file channel) lets PRISM standardize a machine-readable tool list for byte-compare proving.

surfaces.label: Filter comments with advanced trigger
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Tool List > Tool List Setup
surfaces.path: Setup > File Types > Tool List > Filter comments with advanced trigger
surfaces.action: Regular Expression used to scan/filter comment lines (by default comment lines above the tool trigger) so only matching text becomes the tool description, e.g. [A-Z0-9 ]+ to strip banner asterisks.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Ensures the tool descriptions the post writes as comments are extracted cleanly, so the generated tool list's descriptions can be compared to a golden reference.

surfaces.label: Tool List scan options (checkboxes)
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Tool List > Tool List Setup
surfaces.path: Setup > File Types > Tool List > options
surfaces.action: Boolean scan/format options controlling how tools are listed.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: These normalization options (sort, ignore magazine info, ignore leading zeros) determine whether two functionally-equal tool lists byte-match — set them consistently for deterministic golden-vs-actual tool-list comparison.
fields: Sort tool list (list each tool once)
Advanced Tool trigger: Scan two lines at a time

surfaces.label: Tool list template path
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Tool List > Tool List Setup
surfaces.path: Setup > File Types > Tool List > Tool list template
surfaces.action: Path to the tool-list template file; folder icon picks the file, adjacent icon opens it for editing. Bundled templates: Toollist.txt (simple), NewToolList.txt (advanced), NewToolListHtmlSample.txt (HTML sample) in %AppData%/Roaming/CIMCO 2026/CIMCOEdit/SYS.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: The template is a plain text file (file channel) with [CONFIG_BEGIN]/[HEADER_BEGIN] sections (TOOL_TRIGGER_REGEX, COMMENT_START, NUMBER_OF_COMMENTS, EXTRACT_FROM_TOOL_COMMENT, $TOOLINFO/$INFOn vars) — editing it lets PRISM emit a deterministic machine-readable tool list for post proving without the GUI.

surfaces.label: Tool trigger
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Tool List > Tool List Setup
surfaces.path: Setup > File Types > Tool List > Tool trigger
surfaces.action: Character/string CIMCO matches to identify a tool change in the NC (e.g. 'T' for T01). Can be a Regular Expression via the Advanced icon.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: This trigger must match the post's emitted tool-change syntax; if the generated tool list is empty, the post's tool output does not match the trigger — a concrete proving failure signal.

surfaces.label: $TOOL1 / $TOOL2 Trigger
surfaces.area: Editor Setup > Tool List > Tool List Setup
surfaces.path: Setup > File Types > Tool List > $TOOL1/$TOOL2 Trigger
surfaces.action: Advanced (regex) triggers that populate the $TOOL1/$TOOL2 variables, e.g. R<[0-9]+> captures R33 from 'T1 5MM DRILL R33' into $TOOL1.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Lets the tool list capture post-specific fields (e.g. tool-length offset registers) so the generated list can be compared field-by-field against golden.

surfaces.label: Cutter Allowance
surfaces.path: Backplot > Simulation > Settings > Collision Settings > Cutter Allowance
surfaces.action: How far the cutter may penetrate the workpiece before a collision is reported (e.g. 0.1mm), to suppress STL-triangle false positives.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Tolerance band that prevents false-positive collision fails from model meshing noise when proving a post; tune to the model accuracy.

surfaces.label: Hidden model collisions
surfaces.path: Backplot > Simulation > Settings > Collision Settings > Hidden model collisions
surfaces.action: ON = collisions checked even for hidden models (all detected); OFF = collisions for hidden models ignored.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Ensures hidden-but-important geometry (fixtures hidden for visibility) still counts in the crash proof when ON.

surfaces.label: Collision checking per model
surfaces.path: Backplot > Simulation > Settings > Collision Settings > Collision checking per model
surfaces.action: Find One = detect one collision per model-pair type (e.g. tool/workpiece, C-axis/Z-axis); Find All = detect all collisions for all model pairs (slower). 'Per model' = per model pair.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Controls completeness of the collision proof: Find All gives the exhaustive crash list for a posted program; Find One is the fast smoke-test.

surfaces.label: Collision Step Size
surfaces.path: Backplot > Simulation > Settings > Collision Settings > Collision Step Size
surfaces.action: Distance between sample points along the toolpath at which collision checks run. Smaller = more accurate/slower, larger = faster but may miss collisions.
surfaces.postProvingRelevance: Accuracy knob for collision proof: a small step size is required to reliably catch transient crashes in a posted program.
